papers.title: Conservative geometric functors via purity
papers.abstract: We establish a criterion for determining when a family of geometric functors is jointly conservative through the lens of purity in compactly generated triangulated categories. We introduce the notion of pure descendability and we apply it to two particular situations involving sequential limits of ring spectra.

papers.title: An introduction to discrete dynamics in condensed sets: orbits, periodic loci, and arithmetic examples
papers.abstract: We formulate discrete dynamics internally in the topos Cond of condensed sets. For an endomorphism $f\colon X\to X$, we construct orbit quotients, backward histories, preimage trees, and periodic loci as objects evaluated on profinite parameter spaces. The framework recovers global-section dynamics, fully faithfully embeds compact Hausdorff systems, characterizes the invertible extension, and is compatible with inverse limits. It organizes $p$-adic congruence towers and shows, for a Cantor-type non-Archimedean Julia set, that classical periodic points can be dense although the internal periodic locus is not isomorphic to the compact condensed Julia set.

papers.title: FRT presentation of the $q$-Onsager comodule algebra and refined $q$-characters
papers.abstract: We introduce a concept of counital comodule algebra $(B,\delta_B,\epsilon_B)$ over a Hopf ${\mathbb K}$-algebra $H$, where $\delta_B: B\rightarrow B \otimes H$ and $\epsilon_B: B\rightarrow {\mathbb K}$ are coaction and counit homomorphisms, respectively. This structure gives a canonical (counital) comodule algebra map $\iota_B: B \rightarrow H$. In this paper, we study in details the case $B=O_q$, and $H$ is the quantum loop algebra ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$ for ${\mathbb K}={\mathbb C}$. Here, $O_q$ is the $q$-Onsager algebra with four presentations: (i) the $q$-Dolan-Grady type; (ii) the alternating type; (iii) the root vectors type; (iv) the Drinfeld type. For $(O_q,\delta_{O_q},\epsilon_{O_q})$, in fact a 3-parameter family of counital comodule algebras, we establish a Faddeev-Reshetikhin-Takhtajan (FRT) type presentation, which is written in terms of a K-operator satisfying a reflection algebra relation. The coaction $\delta_{O_q}$ (resp. $\iota_{O_q}$) sends the K-operator to a `dressed' K-operator (resp. K-matrix) using Ding-Frenkel type L-operators of ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$; the counit $\epsilon_{O_q}$ sends the K-operator to the most general (non-diagonal) solution of the reflection equation. The FRT presentation allows to compute the image via $\delta_{O_q}$ and $\iota_{O_q}$ of the generating functions of $O_q$ for each presentation (ii)-(iv). Moreover, the images of Lu-Wang's generating functions of $O_q$ in the so-called Drinfeld second realization ${}^{Dr}\!{\cal L}U_qsl_2$ are obtained, as well as their images via the (ordinary) coproduct of ${}^{Dr}\!{\cal L}U_qsl_2$, which enhance two theorems by Prze\'zdziecki. Finally, we apply our FRT presentation to the construction of new type $q$-characters for ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$, in imaginary root vectors of $O_q$, refining those of Frenkel-Reshetikhin, and we explain representation-theoretic meaning of such refining.

papers.title: Multiplicativity of the Serre Spectral Sequence in Homotopy Type Theory
papers.abstract: Working in homotopy type theory, we define relative homotopy groups and give three equivalent definitions of the product on these groups. Using this product, we establish the multiplicativity of the cohomological Serre spectral sequence. We show a connection between the homotopy product and the cup-product in cohomology, which leads to the classically familiar description of the starting page of the spectral sequence as a tensor product of graded rings. As applications, we compute cohomology rings of several classifying spaces and loop spaces of spheres.

papers.title: $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded norms for de Rham-Witt forms
papers.abstract: We make two case studies of $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded homotopy in connection with $p$-adic cohomology. First, we identify the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf T)$-graded $\mathrm{TC}^-$ and $\mathrm{TP}$ of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings as multi-Rees algebras for the Nygaard and $\phi^\bullet(I)$-adic filtrations. We additionally compute $E^{h\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ and $E^{t\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ when $E$ is a general even $\mathbf E_\infty$-ring with $\mathbf T$-action, and compute $(\mathrm{TR}^n)^{h\mathbf T/C_{p^n}}_\bigstar$ in terms of iterated Nygaard filtrations. Next, we compute the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf Z_p)^\land$-graded $\mathrm{TR}$ of smooth algebras over a perfectoid base, providing a pushout of the works of Hesselholt and Angeltveit-Gerhardt along the base case $\mathbf F_p$. Using this, we extend Angeltveit's Norm map of Witt vectors to the de Rham-Witt complex, which participates in a "Witt coordinates" decomposition of the $p$-primary Adams operations.

papers.title: Motivic Mirror Symmetry for Sink-recurrent Cluster Varieties
papers.abstract: We prove motivic mirror symmetry for full-rank sink-recurrent cluster varieties. We allow skew-symmetrizable principal parts and invert all frozen variables. The rational geometric motive of such a variety is isomorphic to the additive orbifold motive of the mirror stack of Hu and Shende. This gives comparisons of cohomology, higher Chow groups, and algebraic $K$-theory with rational coefficients. The proof combines quantum deformation with the splitting of these motives into Tate summands. For really full-rank skew-symmetric seeds, a finite \'{e}tale morphism realizes the comparison. We also study this geometric comparison in families over the projective line.

papers.title: On Poincar\'e spaces which are not manifolds
papers.abstract: This expository note gives a short derivation of the classical Spivak normal fibration formula for the total space of a spherical fibration over a Poincar\'e duality space. We review the associated smooth, PL, and topological manifold realization criteria and illustrate them with examples from the stable stems. The principal application combines these criteria with the completed solution of the Kervaire invariant problem to identify the exceptional stems in a specified family of three cell Poincar\'e spaces.

papers.title: Perfect loops of proper schemes
papers.abstract: We study the perfect loop space $LX$ of a proper scheme $X$ over a local field $F$. We show that if $X$ contains a rational curve, then $LX$ is not ind-representable, even in a very weak sense. We also show that if $X$ admits a proper model $\mathfrak{X}$ over the integers $\mathcal{O}$ of $F$, whose geometric special fiber does not contain rational curves, then $L^+\mathfrak{X} \stackrel{\sim}{\to} LX$ is an isomorphism via the natural map, where $L^+\mathfrak{X}$ denotes the perfect positive loop space (jet scheme) of $\mathfrak{X}$. In particular, $LX$ is a scheme in this case.

papers.title: A tale of two periodicities
papers.abstract: We provide a common explanation for two 4-periodic phenomena arising in the study of connective real K-theory: first, the family of twists of ko over $B\mathbb Z/2$, and second, the torsion in the Picard group of $Q_1$-local $\mathcal A(1)$-modules. These phenomena have been previously studied, as they lead to 4-periodic patterns in Smith homomorphisms, resp. in the ko-homology of $(B\mathbb Z/2)^n$. In this paper, we exhibit both of these 4-periodicities as consequences of an isomorphism of two extraspecial groups of order 32.

papers.title: Coarse Embeddings Beyond Doubling: Persistence Diagrams and Multiparameter Modules
papers.abstract: We study coarse embeddings into Hilbert space and the asymptotic dimension of spaces of persistence diagrams and multiparameter persistence modules. We replace doubling, the usual hypothesis for landmark embeddings, by admissible tent covers of bounded multiplicity at every scale: stacking them across dyadic scales gives an explicit $1$-Lipschitz coarse embedding, with lower gauge $c\sqrt{\tau t}$, or nearly linear for slowly decaying weights, and the same covers bound the asymptotic dimension by the multiplicity. The spaces of persistence diagrams are not doubling but carry such covers, and for diagrams with $n$ points our covers improve the constant of the known landmark embedding by a factor exponential in $n$. Slice by slice, the construction embeds multiparameter modules with boundedly many bars per slice under the matching distance on any finite net of slices, a class that contains the modules with at most $n$ generators. Bounding bars or persistent Betti numbers instead of generators fails: two-parameter modules with one bar on every slice have infinite asymptotic dimension, and neither they nor the modules of bounded support and bounded rank admit a coarse embedding into Hilbert space, under the matching or the interleaving distance.

papers.title: Compact branch sets and injectivity of proper branched coverings
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that a proper continuous open discrete map from the open unit ball $B^n$ onto a domain in $\R^n$ with $n\geq5$ is a homeomorphism whenever its branch set is compact. This answers Vuorinen's question affirmatively in every dimension $n\ge5.$ In dimension four, we also show that, under the additional assumption of quasiregularity, the map is a quasiconformal homeomorphism. Together with the three-dimensional theorem of Kauranen, Luisto and Tengvall, these results answer the quasiregular question posed as Problem~7.66 in the collections of Barth--Brannan--Hayman and Hayman--Lingham in every dimension $n\ge3$.

papers.title: Discrete Configuration Spaces of Simplex Skeleta: a Middle-Dimensional Manifold Phenomenon
papers.abstract: For a simple graph $\Gamma$ without loops and an integer $n\geq2$, Abrams showed in his Ph.D. thesis that the discrete configuration space $DConf(\Gamma,n)$ is homeomorphic to a closed $n$-manifold if and only if $n=2$ and $\Gamma$ is $K_5$ or $K_{3,3}$, the two minimal obstructions to graph planarity. We show that this manifold property persists for the infinite family of discrete configuration spaces obtained by replacing the Kuratowski graphs with the $d$-skeleton of the simplex of dimension $2d+2$, thus recovering Abrams' $K_5$ case when $d=1$. Our manifold recognition argument relies on a recursive application of Whitehead's theorem that collapsible PL manifolds are PL balls, combined with Forman's discrete Morse theory. The resulting construction produces an infinite family of combinatorial spheres that contains the Legendre polytope boundaries and is closed under taking vertex links.

papers.title: Fundamental Groups of Permutation Complexes
papers.abstract: We present an elementary argument showing that fundamental groups of permutation complexes are free. Hence, $\mathbb{R} P^2$ cannot be realized by a permutation complex, answering a question of Chach\'olski, Levi and Meshulam.

papers.title: Global Green-Schwarz response on quaternionic sphere bundles
papers.abstract: Local anomaly polynomials describe local variations, but a normalized Green-Schwarz phase also depends on global background data. We explain this dependence for ten-dimensional three-sphere bundles of quaternionic lines over closed spin seven-manifolds. The backgrounds retain two specified $\mathrm{Spin}(16)$ gauge bundles and an integral differential trivialization on the base, including its boundary identifications. The trivialized class is the sum of half the first Pontryagin class of the tangent bundle and the second Chern class of the quaternionic line's underlying complex bundle. For these backgrounds, the calculation combines a generally nonzero local Green-Schwarz integral with a real eta invariant evaluated by a twelve-dimensional Atiyah-Patodi-Singer filling. Together, these terms determine an integral relative characteristic number; the additive response is one third of that number, modulo integers. When the base's third and fourth rational cohomology groups vanish, the response equals eight times the Crowley-Goette invariant, without assuming that the base is simply connected. A calibration using the actual quaternionic line bundle gives additive value one third on $\mathrm{Sp}(2)$, recovering the known third-root phase. Distinct integral String data on one fixed ten-manifold give all three phase values, showing which global background information the response can detect. The physical identifications retain their prescribed fermion data, while the separate application to integral topological modular forms and vertex operator superalgebras requires compatible integral lifts. The response calculation constructs neither a microscopic realization nor an equivalence of complete theories.

papers.title: On the homotopy automorphism group of simply-connected homology $\mathbb C \mathrm P^3$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we compute the group of homotopy equivalences of closed, smooth, simply connected $6$-manifolds whose integral homology groups are isomorphic to whose of the complex projective space $\mathbb C \mathrm P^3$, building on computations of their mapping class groups.

papers.title: On the monotonicity of amenable category for geometric 4-manifolds and their connected sums
papers.abstract: We show that the amenable category is monotone with respect to the domination relation for geometric $4$-manifolds and their connected sums.

papers.title: Persistence landscape velocity: Closed formulas and a topological probe of quantum criticality
papers.abstract:
We introduce the landscape velocity $\xi$, a scalar measure of variation of a parameter-dependent persistence landscape. For families of finite barcodes whose bars are all born at the fixed filtration value $0$, we show that $\xi$ is the $L^2$ speed of the landscape curve where the sorted death times are differentiable and derive an exact closed formula that requires no persistence landscape at all: the death times of the barcodes, as functions of the parameter, suffice. For the velocity of the empirical mean of several landscapes we also prove a closed formula which, again, strikingly requires neither the empirical mean landscape nor any of the individual landscapes, only the individual barcodes.
  As an application, we revisit Olsthoorn's persistent homology analysis of the transverse-field Ising chain. Whereas his approach uses different homology degrees and summaries depending on the boundary conditions, ours uses $H_0$ only and a single rule: the position of the maximum of $\xi$. This rule locates the quantum critical point for both periodic and open boundary conditions, and for both mutual-information and correlator-based dissimilarities. The position of the maximum converges to the critical point faster than all the estimators we can extract from Olsthoorn's work. In the 4 scenarios considered (different boundary conditions and different dissimilarity matrices), the peak of the normalized velocity becomes increasingly pronounced with system size, with observed logarithmic growth. This logarithmic growth is proved for periodic boundaries with correlator dissimilarity under stated hypotheses, identifying landscape velocity as a singular topological response to quantum criticality.

papers.title: An invariant higher index pairing under Morita equivalence for proper \'etale groupoids
papers.abstract: For suitable proper \'etale groupoids, we study a part of the higher index that is invariant under Morita equivalence. We capture this part by a pairing between cyclic homology classes associated with isotropy groups and cyclic cohomology classes of the groupoid convolution algebra. We show that the pushforward is compatible with the maps induced by essential equivalences. This gives a numerical invariant depending only on the Morita equivalence class of the groupoid. In the case of a finite group action, we relate the resulting pairing to the equivariant index and to the Atiyah-Bott fixed-point formula.

papers.title: On the index of two-dimensional elliptic end-periodic operators
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the index problem for elliptic end-periodic differential operators on a two-dimensional manifold with a cylindrical end. We define the topological index as the sum of the contribution of the interior symbol, expressed by an Atiyah--Singer type integral, and the contribution of the limit operator, expressed in terms of the Melrose type eta-invariant and a correction term that depends on the lower order terms of the limit operator. We prove the homotopy invariance of the topological index, which allows us to reduce the original problem to the study of operators of a simpler form by employing $K$-theoretic methods.

papers.title: $(G,\mu)$-Windows and Deformations of $(G,\mu)$-Displays
papers.abstract: Let $k_0$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$, let $G$ be a smooth affine group scheme over $\mathbb{Z}_p$, and let $\mu$ be a cocharacter of $G_{W(k_0)}$ such that the set of $\mu$-weights of $\Lie G$ is a subset of $\{-1,0,1,2,\dots\}$. We prove that the groupoid of adjoint nilpotent $(G,\mu)$-displays as in \cite[Definition 1.0.1]{pappas}, \cite{lau2} and \cite[Definition 3.16]{E7} is equivalent to the groupoid of $(G,\mu)$-windows, which are the generalizations of windows as in \cite[Definition 5.1]{langer2} and \cite[Definition 3.3.1]{E7}.

papers.title: $\lambda_g$-Integrals on triple, one-part admissible covers
papers.abstract: We effectively compute all intersection numbers of the form $\lambda_g\psi^d$ on moduli spaces of genus $g$ admissible covers with one point of full ramification and two additional branch points with arbitrary profile. We encode these invariants in appropriate generating functions, which we relate to the Hamiltonians of the KdV hierarchy.

papers.title: A depth-zero principal-series block whose Hecke algebra has a non-trivial two-cocycle
papers.abstract: Recently the authors have shown that every Hecke algebra associated to a type constructed by Kim and Yu is isomorphic to a Hecke algebra for a depth-zero type. An example in the literature has been suggested as a counterexample to this result. We show that the example is not a counterexample, and exhibit some of its interesting properties, e.g., we show that a principal series, depth-zero type can have a Hecke algebra with non-trivial two-cocyle, a phenomenon that many did not expect could occur.

papers.title: A family of finite dimensional Hopf algebras over $\mathbb{C}$ with varying algebra structure
papers.abstract: We construct an algebraic one-parameter family of complex Hopf algebras of dimension \(1024\), with fixed coalgebra, whose underlying associative algebras vary in a continuous family of isomorphism classes. Four multiplication lines in the second radical layer of a distinguished block recover the \(j\)-invariant of the elliptic curve given by the equation \(y^2=x(x-1)(x-t^2).\) This answers negatively the finiteness question of Etingof and Gelaki concerning algebra types of Hopf algebras of fixed dimension.

papers.title: A Lefschetz Alternative for Real Characters on Smooth Quasi-Projective Varieties
papers.abstract: We establish a Lefschetz alternative for real characters on smooth complex quasi-projective varieties, extending Simpson's classical theorem beyond the compact K\"ahler setting. More precisely, for a nonzero real character of the fundamental group of a smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety, either the character factors through a holomorphic fibration onto a Riemann orbifold with connected general fiber, or every level set of an associated primitive function on the corresponding covering is connected and its inclusion induces a surjection onto the fundamental group of the covering. Our approach combines logarithmic holomorphic $1$-forms with a geometric flow construction to overcome the difficulties arising from noncompactness. Meanwhile, we prove a quasi-projective analogue of the Napier--Ramachandran theorem, showing that an epimorphism onto $\Z $ whose kernel is not finitely generated must factor through a hyperbolic Riemann orbifold. As applications, we derive several new restrictions on the structure of quasi-projective groups.

papers.title: A LOWER BOUND FOR THE FILLING AREA OF THE CIRCLE
papers.abstract: We establish a universal lower bound for the area of orientable Riemannian fillings of the circle.

papers.title: A Parity Theorem for Reverse-Complement-Invariant Minimum Decycling Sets in q-ary de Bruijn Graphs
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a finite alphabet with a fixed-point-free involutive complement, and let reverse complement act on the directed de Bruijn graph $B(q,k)$ by reversing a word and complementing every letter. We prove that a reverse-complement-invariant ordinary minimum decycling set exists if and only if $k$ is even, for every integer $k\geq2$. This simultaneously covers the binary alphabet and the DNA alphabet with $A\leftrightarrow T$ and $C\leftrightarrow G$. For odd $k$, a primitive rotation cycle joins two reverse-complement-fixed lower states in opposite directions. Disjoint complementary alphabet pairs force at least $q$ deletions beyond the ordinary minimum. For even $k$, choose injective antisymmetric real weights on the alphabet and form a weighted cyclotomic selector. We prove that arbitrary representatives on its zero-embedding rotation cycles preserve acyclicity, resolve those ties equivariantly, and establish the exact defect identity $ \mathbf{1}_{\operatorname{RC}(M)}-\mathbf{1}_M=\nabla\chi . $ A finite sequence of legal full-alphabet source firings removes this nonnegative symmetric defect two coordinates at a time. We also identify a self-dual spectral ideal that gives a deterministic direct selector, rather than a simulated firing path. For integer weights, membership is decidable with polynomial bit complexity. The executable finite panel in the repository checks the binary specialization only; it is convention-level assurance and is not used in the all-order proof.

papers.title: A proof of a conjecture of Cazenave on graph eigenvalues
papers.abstract: We prove Cazenave's conjecture $\mu_2^2\ge4\lambda_2+1$ for connected graphs, where $\lambda_2$ and $\mu_2$ are the second largest adjacency and Laplacian eigenvalues. We also characterize equality in this inequality and in the linear bound $\mu_2\ge\lambda_2+1$.

papers.title: A relative trace formula for the orthogonal Gan-Gross-Prasad model and the proof of its fundamental lemma
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a comparison of relative trace formulas to study the Gan--Gross--Prasad conjecture. We unfold the relative trace formulas, match their regular orbits, and formulate the corresponding fundamental lemma and smooth transfer conjecture. Finally, we prove the fundamental lemma for the unit element of the Hecke algebra.

papers.title: A silting theorem for extended module categories
papers.abstract: We generalize the silting theorem of Buan and Zhou to extended module categories. For a $(d+1)$-term silting object $\mathbf{P}$ over a proper $d$-truncated non-positive dg algebra $A$, we construct a $(d+1)$-term silting object $\mathbf{Q}$ over the $d$-truncated dg endomorphism algebra $B$ of $\mathbf{P}$. The $s$-torsion pairs induced by $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$ yield equivalences of Brenner-Butler type between the torsion class on either side and the torsion-free class on the other. There is also a dg algebra homomorphism from $A$ to the $d$-truncated dg endomorphism algebra of $\mathbf{Q}$, which is a quasi-isomorphism if and only if $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf{P},\mathbf{P}[i])=0$ for all $i\leq-d$. Moreover, we describe Auslander-Reiten theory in ${d\text{-}\operatorname{mod}\!B}$ in terms of that in ${d\text{-}\operatorname{mod}\!A}$.

papers.title: A uniform decomposition theorem for invariant differential operators on imprimitive complex reflection groups G(r,p,n)
papers.abstract: {We study the module structure of the polynomial ring, localized at the discriminant, over the ring of differential operators on the ring of invariants of the imprimitive complex reflection group $G(r,p,n)$, describing its simple components with explicit generators given by the higher Specht polynomials of Ariki--Terasoma--Yamada. The proof rests on a Jacobian lemma computing the discriminant of $G(r,p,n)$, combined with a double-centralizer argument. As particular cases ($r=2$, $p=2$ or $p=1$) we recover, and considerably shorten, the known decomposition theorems for the real reflection groups $W(D_n)$ and $W(B_n)$; we also treat $G(r,r,n)$ and $G(r,1,n)$ explicitly, with worked examples ($D_2$, $D_3$, $B_2$) and their central idempotents. Finally, applying the Galois descent equivalence of categories of Nonkan\'e to $G(r,p,n)$ for the first time gives a second, generator-free description of the simple summands as twisted invariants.}

papers.title: A Zariski-Open Family of Proper Septic Polynomials with Full Traceless Images
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. We identify a $762$-dimensional space of proper multilinear degree-seven polynomials in the third power of the commutator ideal, with zero formal cyclic trace and annihilated by every repeated-input identification of type $(3,3,1)$. A nonempty Zariski-open subset of this space consists of polynomials $p$ whose sets of individual matrix values satisfy $p(M_n(K)^7)=\mathfrak{sl}_n(K)$ for every $n\geq3$. The ambient proper and formal trace-zero spaces have dimensions $1260$ and $1049$, respectively. An explicit polynomial certifies nonemptiness of this coefficient-open family. The proof combines a symmetric-group decomposition, exact finite determinant witnesses, an additive-size argument and a separate $3\times3$ matrix argument.

papers.title: Abelian categories and double d\'ecalage
papers.abstract: We show that an additive category is abelian if and only if its functorial nerve is a double d\'ecalage of a pseudo-simplicial object in Cat. In this characterization, the canonical isomorphism between the image and coimage is encoded by a coherent pseudo-simplicial identity.

papers.title: Actual images and local fibers in the second commutator layer
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and let $J$ be the commutator ideal of the free associative algebra. We prove that, for every proper multilinear polynomial $f\in J^2\setminus J^3$ and every $n\ge3$, the set of values of $f$ on $M_n(K)$ is $\mathfrak{sl}_n(K)$ if $\tr f\equiv0$, and $M_n(K)$ otherwise. In the first case the evaluation map is smooth at an input with nonzero rank-one square-zero value. In the second case it is flat at such an input, with a local complete-intersection fiber of the expected dimension. The theorem allows arbitrary proper multilinear corrections of the same degree in $J^3$. We use restrictions to two active variables with commuting passive inputs and detect the first nonzero trace term on the exact fiber of the traceless projection.

papers.title: Adaptive visualization for enumerative problems
papers.abstract: We present an adaptive visualization framework and its implementation in the julia package AdaptiveVisualization.jl. Our algorithm visualizes functions using an adaptive sampling procedure that concentrates the evaluation budget at interesting regions of the domain. We illustrate our package on our main application: visualizing parameter spaces of enumerative problems.

papers.title: Algebraic cycles on some Fano varieties with Hodge structure of level one and of Calabi-Yau type
papers.abstract: We study Chow groups and \'etale motivic cohomology groups of smooth complete intersections with Hodge structures of level one, classified by Deligne and Rapoport, with particular attention to fivefolds. We extend these results to an \'etale motivic context and recover an analogous finite-dimensionality in the sense of Kimura. We then turn to quartic double fivefolds, which are Fano fivefolds whose middle cohomology is numerically similar to that of a Calabi-Yau threefold. By means of cubic surfaces which are totally ramified along the branch locus, we prove the integral Hodge conjecture for all of them. We also show that the comparison maps between their Chow groups and \'etale Chow groups are isomorphisms except possibly in codimension three, where we describe the kernel and the cokernel in terms of Bloch-Ogus cohomology and, via a Sarkisov link, of the unramified cohomology of a cubic surface over the function field of $\mathbb{P}^3$.

papers.title: All-genus mirror symmetry for the type-$D$ minimal resolution Calabi-Yau threefold
papers.abstract: Let $Y$ be the product of a minimal resolution of a binary dihedral surface singularity with an equivariant line, with volume-preserving scalar action. We identify its stable equivariant descendant Gromov--Witten theory and its free energies in genus at least two with the sign-sector topological recursion of the degenerate type-$D$ relativistic Toda spectral curve. The $R-$matrix calibration is determined at a partial large-radius limit, where the trivalent exceptional curve retains a nonzero K\"ahler parameter, while the remaining parameters vanish. The limiting theory on the mirror side is a sum of twisted point theories and the local $(-2,0)$ curve theory. Moreover, we identify the equivariant K-group supported on the surface zero section with an integral relative homology group of the mirror. Explicit cycles for the dual tautological bundles realize their Gamma central charges and all stable Gamma-framed descendants.

papers.title: Almost all $k$-Markov numbers are unique
papers.abstract: For every fixed nonnegative integer $k$, we prove that almost every positive integral solution of [x^2+y^2+z^2+k(xy+xz+yz)= 3(k+1)xyz]is uniquely determined, up to permutation, by its largest coordinate.

papers.title: An Algebraic Representation Theorem for Linear GENEOs in Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Geometric and Topological Deep Learning enhance machine learning by exploiting geometric and topological structures in data. In this context, Group Equivariant Non-Expansive Operators (GENEOs) provide a principled framework for encoding symmetries and designing efficient, interpretable neural architectures. Originally introduced in Topological Data Analysis and later adopted in Deep Learning, GENEOs unify geometric and topological approaches and include, as a special case, the operator computing persistence diagrams. Their theoretical foundations rely on group actions, equivariance, and compactness properties of operator spaces. GENEOs are defined between data spaces endowed with transformation groups, referred to as perception pairs. While previous representation results characterized linear GENEOs acting on identical perception pairs, many applications require operators between heterogeneous ones. In this work, we introduce and prove a new algebraic representation theorem for linear GENEOs acting between different perception pairs. Under mild assumptions on data domains and group actions, this result provides a complete characterization of such operators and implicitly yields a computational method to generate all linear GENEOs between two perception pairs. The proof combines tools from the theory of stochastic matrices, group actions, and invariant measures. In our paper, we also show that the space of linear GENEOs is compact and convex, making easier their use for learning and optimization. Our new theorem enlarges the applicability of GENEOs, and allows for their composition with a broader class of current architectures. We show this with an application in image reconstruction.

papers.title: An analytic lower bound for the cubic-lattice dimer constant
papers.abstract: We prove that the close-packed dimer entropy per site $\ell_3$ of the simple cubic lattice satisfies $\ell_3\ge \frac12\log\frac{3125}{1296}+\frac{47}{10000}=0.444775842629\ldots.$ This exceeds the previous best published lower bound, obtained by Csikvári of $0.441075842629\ldots$. The proof uses finite matching inequalities and elementary integration, without numerical quadrature or a computational certificate.

papers.title: An Eilenberg-Watts Theorem and Morita localization for Hilbert modules over $C^*$-categories
papers.abstract: Hilbert modules over a $C^*$-category were first defined by Mitchener, who also proved that they form a $C^*$-category. An Eilenberg-Watts theorem for Hilbert modules over $C^*$-algebras was proved by Blecher. We follow a similar path to prove an Eilenberg-Watts theorem for Hilbert modules over $C^*$-categories and characterize equivalences of categories of Hilbert modules as being given by tensoring with imprimitivity bimodules. We employ our results to prove several equivalences of bicategories of $C^*$-algebras and $C^*$-categories, and to exhibit a Morita localization of the category of locally small $C^*$-categories.

papers.title: An explicit basis for the unipotent Specht modules of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$
papers.abstract: For each partition $\lambda$ of $n$ we construct an explicit basis of the unipotent Specht module $S^\lambda$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, defined recursively over horizontal strips. Each basis vector is $g\,x_\tau$, where $\tau$ is a semistandard tableau of shape $\lambda$, $x_\tau$ is obtained from a Steinberg-type vector by alternately applying a permutation matrix and a Fourier sum over a unitriangular group, and $g$ runs over an explicit set of coset representatives. Grouping the basis by the standardization of $\tau$ gives exactly $q^{\mathrm{maj}(s^T)}$ vectors for each standard tableau $s$, which is the numerical form of the Dipper-James standard basis problem. The same family is a basis over every field containing a nontrivial $p$th root of unity, including fields whose characteristic divides $|\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)|$, and a subfamily chosen layer by layer gives a basis of the simple quotient $D^\lambda$. We also give a basis of the $U$-fixed vectors of $S^\lambda$ and computed values of $\dim D^\lambda$ for $\mathrm{GL}_n(2)$.

papers.title: Another Proof of Laurent Positivity for Generalized Cluster Algebras
papers.abstract: We prove Laurent positivity in the original exchange coefficients for skew-symmetrizable Chekhov–Shapiro generalized cluster algebras of arbitrary finite rank.

papers.title: Another proof of Laurent positivity for skew-symmetric quantum cluster algebras
papers.abstract: We give another proof of Laurent positivity for skew-symmetric quantum cluster algebras.

papers.title: Associated varieties of integral minimal highest weight modules
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex simple Lie algebra and $L(\lambda)$ be a simple highest weight module of $\mathfrak{g}$ with highest weight $\lambda-\rho$, where $\rho$ is half the sum of positive roots. A simple $\mathfrak{g}$-module $L_w:=L(-w\rho)$ is called integral minimal if the associated variety of its annihilator ideal equals the closure of the unique minimal special nilpotent orbit. In this paper, we find that the associated variety of any integral minimal module $L_w$ is irreducible and equal to the orbital variety corresponding to a minimal-length element in the Kazhdan--Lusztig right cell containing $w$.

papers.title: Autocorrelation Phase Lattices on Cyclic Groups: Unit Supports, 2pq Orbit Profiles, and Binary Reconstruction
papers.abstract: For a finite cyclic group and an exact Fourier support $S$, we study the lattice $\mathcal{L}_{\le d}(S)$ generated by zero-sum relations of length at most $d$ inside the full relation lattice $K(S)$. Its closing degree is both a local separating degree and the order at which every invisible phase ratio becomes a translation character. For the exact unit support of every even cyclic group, we compute $$ \mathbb{Z}^{U_{n}}/\mathcal{L}_{\le4}(U_{n})\cong \begin{cases} \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z},&3\nmid n,\\ \mathbb{Z}\oplus\mathbb{Z}/(n/6)\mathbb{Z},&6\mid n. \end{cases} $$ Moreover $\mathcal{L}_{\le5}(U_{n})=\mathcal{L}_{\le4}(U_{n})$. Thus fourth- and fifth-order rational ambiguity coincide: fourth order reconstructs up to translation when $3\nmid n$, while for $n=6m$ the complete surviving family has normalized ratios parameterized by norm-one elements of $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_6)$, modulo the residual translation subgroup $\mu_6$; order six closes it. For $n=2pq$ with distinct odd primes, we classify every nonempty $\operatorname{Aut}(C_n)$-stable support. The distributions of these 255 supports by closing degree are $$ (1,2,154,80,4,14)\quad(p=3),\qquad (1,2,154,92,4,2)\quad(p,q\ge5). $$ The proof uses seven local CRT presentations, cubic and quartic Skeletons, and explicit depth-five and depth-six obstructions. Galois-equivariant lower-bound ratios show that the lattice, rational-signal and integer-signal closing degrees coincide on every stable support. Finally, for binary indicators, a supportwise crosswalk and a uniform exclusion of all deep supports give $r_{\rm set}(C_{2pq})=4$ under translations. The value is also four for the same oriented analytical deck when outputs are identified up to translation or reflected translation.

papers.title: Automorphisms of Kummer and Artin-Schreier curves defined by Chebyshev polynomials
papers.abstract: Let phi_m be the monic Chebyshev polynomial characterized by phi_m(t + t^-1) = t^m + t^-m. We study the geometric automorphism groups of the smooth projective models of y^n = phi_m(x) and y^p - y = phi_m(x). We classify the hyperelliptic family in genus at least two, in characteristic zero and odd characteristic. For every m >= 5, with p not dividing m in positive characteristic, we determine the projective stabilizer of the roots of phi_m together with infinity. For tame Kummer covers, we describe the normalizer of the cyclic deck group and compute it explicitly for m >= 6. It is the full group when m > 2n. If m >= 3 and n > 2m, the full group has order 2n in characteristic zero and in every characteristic prime to 2nm. The proof uses the dihedral Galois closure of the map to the y-line and Dickson's subgroup classification. In odd characteristic, we also classify all Artin-Schreier curves in the family with genus at least two. For m >= 3 prime to p >= 5, the group has order 2p. In characteristic three, exactly five degrees are exceptional. We give the groups and their actions, and treat the quadratic cases separately.

papers.title: Binary Belief Propagation Fixed Points: Finiteness, Rigidity, and Topological Complexity
papers.abstract: A fixed finite binary Ising model has only finitely many admissible complex belief propagation fixed points, even at degenerate parameter values. Families of positive fixed points obtained by varying external fields can nevertheless have nontrivial topology. We study this distinction through the external-field projection. For a fixed field, we prove finiteness by bounding the pole orders of the magnetizations on a hypothetical complex solution curve. The generic degree on the support graph then bounds the total local multiplicity. A graph has a single smooth real line as its full positive response for every choice of positive couplings, base field, and strictly positive sweep direction exactly when it contains no two vertex-disjoint connected subgraphs of cycle rank at least two. Two such subgraphs suffice to create a circular component. For a plane obtained by varying two vertex fields, connected simple bipartite cubic graphs with one uniform coupling and a universal bound on the fixed fields realize every genus. The minimum number of vertices grows logarithmically in the genus, by a matching algebraic upper bound on Betti numbers. Finally, we certify the complete field discriminant of an eighteen-vertex product model and recover its torus component's genus from the counts of distinct roots on all field cells. The three main theorems, including the logarithmic size bounds, are formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

papers.title: Birational Geometry of K-Moduli Spaces of Genus Four Curves
papers.abstract: We study the wall-crossings for K-moduli spaces of (3,3)-curves on $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$. Together with the boundary polarized Calabi--Yau moduli space, these spaces interpolate between the GIT moduli space of (3,3)-curves and the Baily--Borel compactification of the moduli space of K3 surfaces arising as cyclic triple covers of $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$ branched along such curves. As applications, we describe the corresponding birational models in the Hassett--Keel--Looijenga program and realize the K-moduli space of degree one del Pezzo surfaces through explicit wall-crossings.

papers.title: Bott--Chern and Aeppli Cohomology of toroidal groups
papers.abstract: We compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups of theta toroidal groups in arbitrary dimensions, obtaining explicit dimension formulas and bases in all bidegrees. For general toroidal groups, we determine the Hausdorff reductions of these cohomology groups and show that they coincide with those of theta toroidal groups. We also compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups themselves in certain specific bidegrees, without passing to their Hausdorff reductions.

papers.title: Bounded ratios for Lorentzian matrices
papers.abstract: We study multiplicative inequalities among entries of Lorentzian matrices, referred to as bounded ratios. These inequalities can be viewed as generalizations of the classical Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for mixed volumes. Our main structural result identifies the cone of all bounded ratios on Lorentzian matrices with the dual of the cut cone, a finitely generated integral polyhedral cone extensively studied in metric geometry and graph theory. We examine in detail the pentagonal ratio, which first appears for Lorentzian matrices of size at least five. For Lorentzian matrices of size three, we determine the optimal bounding constants across the entire cone of bounded ratios, obtaining an explicit entropy-like formula.

papers.title: Calligraphs and sphere realizations
papers.abstract: We introduce a recursive procedure for computing the number of realizations of a minimally rigid graph on the sphere up to rotations. We accomplish this by combining two ingredients. The first is a framework that allows us to think of such realizations as of elements of a moduli space of stable rational curves with marked points. The second is the idea of splitting a minimally rigid graph into two subgraphs, called calligraphs, that admit one degree of freedom and that share only a single edge and a further vertex. This idea has been recently employed for realizations of graphs in the plane up to isometries. The key result is that we can associate to a calligraph a triple of natural numbers with a special property: whenever a minimally rigid graph is split into two calligraphs, the number of realizations of the former equals the product of the two triples of the latter, where this product is specified by a fixed quadratic form. These triples and quadratic form codify the fact that we express realizations as intersections of two curves on the blowup of a sphere along two pairs of complex conjugate points.

papers.title: Can small transformers learn the language of Coxeter groups?
papers.abstract: The field of mechanistic interpretability is well-suited to collaborative projects between mathematicians and AI researchers. This work describes one such project. We trained a small transformer to learn the language of the Coxeter group affine A2, best known as the symmetries of the tiling of the Euclidean plane by equilateral triangles. We then formulated and proved a word-theoretic conjecture about affine A2 after observing the attention patterns of the trained model.

papers.title: Cellular free resolutions for normalizations of toric ideals
papers.abstract: For any toric ideal $I$ in a polynomial ring $S$, we provide a combinatorial description of a free resolution of the integral closure of the $S$-module $S/I$. These new complexes arise from an extension of Bayer--Sturmfels' theory of cellular free resolutions. As applications, we unify several constructions for a resolution of the diagonal embedding of a toric variety, and compare the locally free resolutions for toric subvarieties introduced by Hanlon--Hicks--Lazarev and Brown--Erman.

papers.title: Classification of 3-dimensional complex nilmanifolds - Teichm\"uller and moduli spaces
papers.abstract: We classify complex nilmanifolds of dimension three by describing the Teichm\"uller and moduli spaces of left-invariant complex structures for every real six-dimensional nilmanifold.

papers.title: Classification of quasi-lisse simple affine vertex algebras
papers.abstract: We classify all noncritical levels $k$ for which the simple affine vertex algebra $L_k(\mathfrak{g})$ is quasi-lisse, for every finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$. We prove that Fiebig's equivalence between the corresponding noncritical blocks of category $\mathcal{O}$ identifies the relevant parabolic Wakimoto modules and the homomorphisms from the corresponding universal affine vertex algebras. Combining this compatibility with a characterization of semisimple points in associated varieties, we establish that for coprime positive integers $p,q$, $L_{-h^\vee+p/q}(\mathfrak{g})$ is quasi-lisse if and only if $L_{-h^\vee+p/\gcd(q,r)}(\mathfrak{g})$ is quasi-lisse, where $r$ is the lacing number of $\mathfrak{g}$. The classification at the resulting levels is obtained using Drinfeld--Sokolov reduction, singular vectors and relations in the reductions of the maximal ideals of $V^k(\mathfrak{g})$. We also determine the associated varieties at the quasi-lisse levels for all $\mathfrak{g}$ of rank at most six and for $E_7$ and $E_8$.

papers.title: Cohomological Mackey formula for quotient stacks
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct a restriction morphism on the critical cohomology of an equivariant Landau-Ginzburg model associated to a representation of a reductive group equipped with an invariant function. We show a compatibility formula between this restriction map and the induction map considered in earlier work in the form of a Mackey-type formula, thereby giving the critical cohomology the structure of a localized induction-restriction system. In the case of quivers, our formulas give the localized coproduct of Davison for cohomological Hall algebras of quivers with potential.

papers.title: Composition of Sarkisov links between del Pezzo surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that for any two birationally equivalent del Pezzo surfaces of Picard rank one over a perfect field there is a birational map between them such that it is decomposed in a composition of at most two Sarkisov links.

papers.title: Consecutive Divisors of Sums of Fibonacci Polynomials: a Luca–Marques Analogue in Finite-Field Polynomial Rings
papers.abstract: For every prime power $q$ with $\gcd(q,6)=1$, we construct infinitely many pairs of consecutive monic polynomials in $\mathbb{F}_q[T]$ whose product divides the Fibonacci-polynomial sum with upper index one less than their common norm. This gives a function-field counterpart of the divisibility condition in the Luca–Marques theorem on consecutive integral arithmetic means of Fibonacci numbers. A short extension of the construction gives infinitely many triples of consecutive monic polynomials with the same property.

papers.title: Cores and localizations of $(\infty,\infty)$-categories
papers.abstract:
We consider $(\infty,d)$-categories in the limit $d\to \infty$ via the core or localization functors that forget or invert higher non-invertible arrows, respectively. We compare the two resulting $(\infty,1)$-categories of $(\infty,\infty)$-categories and exhibit the localization-limit as a reflective localization of the core-limit.
  Furthermore, we study notions of invertibility that only emerge at $d=\infty$ and give rise to intermediate reflective localizations between the two limits. For example, we characterize coinductive completion and the maps it inverts, and reveal a new separation beyond the one of Henry--Loubaton by showing that even the stronger $\omega$-completeness does not suffice to carve out the localization-limit.

papers.title: Counter-examples to Conjectures on NCCRs via a Reductive McKay Correspondence
papers.abstract: We disprove three conjectures appearing in Van den Bergh's plenary ICM survey, posed by De Deyn and Van den Bergh, which concern the interplay between non-commutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs) and the stringy Euler characteristic. Our counter-examples are applications of a new McKay correspondence for reductive groups that we prove in this paper, extending the classical McKay correspondence for finite groups. We obtain explicit formulas for the stringy $E$-functions of reductive quotients in terms of the Weyl group action and stringy $E$-functions of toric varieties; we also obtain an equivalent formula expressed as an integral of the age function over Weyl-fixed loci of a compact real torus. For symmetric representations, our expressions are related to arithmetic Tutte polynomials, yielding combinatorial formulas for the stringy Euler characteristic.

papers.title: Critical edges in labelled complete graphs
papers.abstract: In a complete graph whose edges have labels 1,...,ell, an edge is critical for a matching if its label is smaller than that of a matching edge sharing an endpoint. The parameter gamma(ell) is the asymptotic worst-case, over labelings, of the smallest critical-edge count obtainable by choosing the matching, normalized by the number of pairs of covered vertices; gamma'(ell) is its perfect-matching version. These parameters arise in bounds for finding cliques in random graphs by edge queries in a prescribed number of rounds. We prove 0.419772820486... <= gamma'(4) <= gamma(4) <= 0.4334035. For every ell >= 2 we give an explicit construction proving gamma'(ell) >= 1/2-1/[4(ell-1)]. We also improve the state-of-the-art upper bounds for general ell, obtaining gamma(ell) <= 1/2-4/(5*2^ell) +O(2^(-3*ell/2)) as ell tends to infinity, together with explicit finite bounds. The proofs of upper bounds compare matchings obtained by local exchanges. The proofs of lower bounds use labelings that are constant on pairs of vertex parts; the stronger four-label construction has six parts and an algebraic value of degree six. Exact-arithmetic verification programs and their data are included for the computer-assisted parts of the proofs.

papers.title: Critical-point-free energy for fractional-Toledo representations
papers.abstract: Let $S_g$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g\ge2$. For a reductive representation $\rho:\pi_1(S_g)\to\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$, let $E_\rho$ be the energy function on Teichm\"uller space associated to equivariant harmonic maps into $\mathrm{CH}^2$. For every positive integer $d$ with $3\nmid d$, all sufficiently large $h$, and every $g>h$, we construct an irreducible reductive representation \[ \rho_{g,h,d}:\pi_1(S_g)\to\mathrm{PU}(2,1) \] with \[ \tau(\rho_{g,h,d})=2h-2-\frac{2d}{3}\notin\mathbb Z, \qquad \mathrm{Crit}(E_{\rho_{g,h,d}})=\varnothing. \] Consequently, the associated branched-minimal-surface forgetful map is not surjective in these nonintegral Toledo components.

papers.title: Cylindricity of log del Pezzo surfaces in characteristic five
papers.abstract: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic five, we prove that a log del Pezzo surface of Picard rank one contains no cylinder if it is not log liftable. We also characterize Du Val del Pezzo surfaces that contain no cylinder in positive characteristic.

papers.title: Decomposable disjoint-union circuits for primitive words
papers.abstract: For every fixed finite alphabet $A$ with at least two letters, we construct smooth decomposable circuits representing the primitive words of each length $n$. The gates are literals, Cartesian products on disjoint position sets, and disjoint unions on equal position sets. The total number of gates and wires is $O_A(n^2 5^{\omega(n)})=n^{2+o(1)}$, and the construction takes $n^{2+o(1)}$ bit operations. Prime periods are expressed as coordinate directions of independent rectangular grids. A recursion at the first nonconstant vertex computes the exact set of failed directions; sharing its continuations gives the size bound. This resolves the primitive-word instance of the circuit question posed by Amarilli, Monet, Raphael, and Salvati. It does not determine whether primitive words form a context-free or a poly-slicewise-unambiguous language. The same circuit bound holds for any union of exact power orders at a fixed length.

papers.title: Derivations tangent to polar discriminants
papers.abstract: We describe the module of logarithmic derivations along the discriminant of a stable polar representation of a reductive algebraic group. It splits into derivations along the fibres of the quotient map and a free summand lifted from logarithmic derivations along the associated branch divisor. This gives a uniform extension of previous results on full adjoint discriminants. We prove that, for visible stable polar actions of semisimple groups with finite generic stabilizer, the discriminant is a free divisor. For stable periodic gradings of arbitrary order with semisimple degree-zero group, we construct explicit Saito matrices from the infinitesimal action and the gradients of basic invariants, which yields determinantal equations for several exceptional discriminants. In particular, starting with exceptional Lie algebras, we provide examples of free discriminants of degrees 60, 120, 126 and 240 for inner gradings and a degree-72 example for an outer one.

papers.title: Derived invariance of the numbers $h^{0,p}(X)$
papers.abstract: Let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be derived equivalent smooth projective varieties over the field of complex numbers. We prove that the numbers $h^{0,p}(X_1)$ and $h^{0,p}(X_2)$ are equal for any $p$.

papers.title: Derived invariance of the space of holomorphic two-forms
papers.abstract:
Let $\Phi:D^b(X)\to D^b(Y)$ be a derived equivalence between smooth projective complex varieties, and let $h=c_1(L)$ for an ample line bundle $L$ on $X$. For $z\in\mathbb{C}$, transporting the cup-product action and evaluating at $e^{zh}$ gives a homomorphism of graded algebras $\Theta^\bullet_{F,z}:H^\bullet(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\to H^\bullet(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $F$ is the cohomological transform of $\Phi$. We prove that $\Theta^\bullet_{F,i}$ is an isomorphism in degrees one and two. In particular, $X$ and $Y$ have the same number of holomorphic two-forms. The proof in degree two uses the Hodge-Riemann bilinear relations on $X$ and on $X\times X$.
  We also prove derived invariance of all Hodge numbers when $K_X$ is trivial and the conjugate of a holomorphic volume form belongs to the subalgebra of $H^\bullet(X,\mathcal O_X)$ generated in degrees one and two. In even dimension, the evaluation isomorphism allows us to compare the ranks of cup product by powers of symplectic two-forms on the Hochschild diagonals. These ranks determine the Hodge numbers individually.

papers.title: Dividends of the BKR Equivalence: Quantifying the Dichotomy for Skyscraper Sheaves
papers.abstract: Let $G\subset \mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb C)$ be a nontrivial finite abelian subgroup and let $\Psi \colon D^b_G(\mathbb{C}^3) \xrightarrow{\sim} D^b(G\operatorname{-}\mathrm{Hilb}(\mathbb{C}^3))$ denote the Bridgeland--King--Reid equivalence. For every nontrivial character $\chi$ of $G$, the transform of the corresponding skyscraper sheaf at the origin has exactly one nonzero cohomology sheaf, in degree $0$ or $-1$. We study the proportion $\mathcal B_0$ of characters for which this degree is zero. Using derived Reid's recipe, we establish the sharp bounds $1/3\leq\mathcal B_0\leq1$. For isolated quotient singularities, the lower bound sharpens to $1/2$, and we exhibit an explicit family of cyclic quotients indexed by positive integers $m$ for which $\mathcal{B}_0 \to 1$ as $m \to \infty$. We show that $\mathcal B_0=1$ precisely when the fiber over the origin has dimension at most one, and relate $\mathcal B_0$ to the Picard rank of $G\operatorname{-}\mathrm{Hilb}(\mathbb{C}^3)$ and the number of compact exceptional divisors of the resolution $G\operatorname{-}\mathrm{Hilb}(\mathbb{C}^3)\rightarrow \mathbb{C}^3/G$. A theorem of Craw--Lin--Yamagishi translates these estimates into bounds for the coordinate facets of the $G$-Hilbert GIT chamber. We discuss how the proportion $\mathcal{B}_0$ adapts to non-abelian finite subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{C})$.

papers.title: Dlab--Ringel standardization in algebraic triangulated categories
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of derived standardly stratified algebras as a connective dg analogue of standardly stratified algebras. To this end, we extend the Dlab--Ringel standardization method to algebraic triangulated categories and show that every basic proper derived standardly stratified algebra arises from this extended method. We establish Ringel duality for derived standardly stratified algebras using silting objects. More precisely, the Ringel dual is again derived standardly stratified, and the corresponding perfect derived categories are related by mutually quasi-inverse contravariant triangle equivalences. We also show that, over an algebraically closed field, a proper derived standardly stratified algebra is smooth if and only if its derived standard modules are exceptional. Finally, we prove that dg algebras given by finite acyclic graded quivers with arrows of non-positive degrees and homogeneous relations are derived standardly stratified with respect to every total order on the vertices.

papers.title: Dominant permutations, positive mixed-variable formulas, and product-splitting equivalence for (double) Schubert polynomials
papers.abstract:
We present new positive combinatorial formulas for triple Schubert coefficients in mixed-variable products of double Schubert polynomials, $\mathfrak{S}_u(x;y)\mathfrak{S}_v(x;z)$, expressed in the $\mathfrak{S}_w(x;y)$ basis, in the case where $u$ is dominant. This result complements earlier results where $v$ was assumed dominant. To generalize further, we introduce a relation on permutations that we call ``domination,'' under which dominant permutations dominate all others. When $u$ dominates $w$, we obtain an explicit positive formula for $c^w_{u,v}(y;z)$, which in particular yields positivity when $u$ and $v$ have separated descents.
  In addition to these new positivity results, we establish a product--splitting equivalence for double Schubert polynomials, relating triple Schubert coefficients to splitting coefficients. This equivalence highlights structural symmetries and provides reduction methods for computing coefficients that are otherwise difficult to access. Taken together, these results extend the range of double Schubert polynomial products for which positivity can be established combinatorially and yield explicit formulas that can be implemented computationally.

papers.title: Eaton Triples, Polar Representations, and Lie Triple Systems
papers.abstract: An Eaton triple consists of a finite dimensional real inner product space, a closed subgroup of its orthogonal group, and a closed convex cone that meets every orbit and satisfies an extremal inner product inequality. In the literature on group majorization and invariant norms it is a standing hypothesis that the triple admits a reduced triple, obtained by restriction to the span of the cone. We prove that this is always the case: the axioms force the span of the cone to be a section of a polar representation, and Gichev's orbit intersection theorem applies. The reduced group is a finite reflection group, crystallographic when the group is connected; Eaton cones are its closed chambers, unique up to the group action; and a compact linear group admits an Eaton cone if and only if its representation is polar with a finite reflection group as Weyl group. For connected groups we construct a Lie triple system on the space, determined by the inner product and the orbits alone, for which the cone is a Weyl chamber; unlike Dadok's orbit equivalence with a symmetric space, it involves no choices.

papers.title: Effective Resistance in Simplicial Complexes: Generalizations and Properties
papers.abstract:
Originally introduced in circuit theory, the notion of effective resistance has been fruitfully exploited in graph theory, where each edge in a graph is understood as a resistor in an electric network. In this context, the effective resistance between two vertices quantifies the total opposition to current flow when a unit current is injected at one vertex and extracted at the other. As such, it encodes rich structural and geometric information about the underlying graph: it satisfies a minimum-energy principle termed Thomson's principle, defines a metric on the vertex set, relates to the topology of the graph through Foster's theorem, and determines the probability of appearance of an edge in a random spanning tree. Generalizations of effective resistance to simplicial complexes have been proposed in several forms, often formulated as matrix products of standard operators associated with the complex.
  We introduce a novel, basis-independent bilinear form, derived from an algebraic reinterpretation of circuit theory, that extends the classical effective resistance from graphs to simplicial complexes. This bilinear form acts on chains and cochains, and in particular, simplices and cosimplices in a simplicial complex. Our framework subsumes and unifies all existing matrix-based formulations of effective resistance. Moreover, we establish higher-order analogues of several fundamental properties known in the graph case: (i) we extend Thomson's principle to our basis-free framework; (ii) we establish metric properties for the effective resistance and its square root on chains and cycles, recovering the classical graph case; (iii) we provide a generalization of Foster's theorem to simplicial complexes; and (iv) we prove a matrix-tree theorem for higher-dimensional spanning trees, linking effective resistance to the probability of appearance of a simplex in random simplicial spanning trees.

papers.title: Embedding Calculus, Goodwillie Calculus and Link Invariants
papers.abstract: We study Goodwillie-Weiss embedding calculus through its relationship with Goodwillie's functor calculus. Specifically, building on a result of Tillmann and Weiss, we construct a functorial complement for \(T_{n}\)-embeddings that takes values in Heuts's categorical \(n\)-excisive approximation of pointed spaces. We also establish an analogue of Stallings' theorem for lower central series in the context of \(T_{n}\)-embeddings of \(P \times I\) into \(D^{d}\) for any compact manifold \(P\). As an application, we show that the embedding tower of string links detects Milnor invariants.

papers.title: Extendability of general prime $K3$ surfaces without Gaussian maps and classification of prime Fano threefolds
papers.abstract: In arXiv:2409.03960 an approach to the question of extendability of projective varieties via degeneration to ribbons was introduced, and in arXiv:2503.12661 it was used to give a new proof of optimal results on the extendability of general non-prime $K3$ surfaces and the classification of non-prime Fano threefolds. In this article we treat the prime case. We give a new proof of the optimal results on the extendability of general prime $K3$ surfaces of every genus, of the classification of prime Fano threefolds of Picard rank one due to Fano, Iskovskikh and Mukai, and of the irreducibility of their Hilbert schemes. This involves degenerations of $K3$ surfaces to ribbons on embedded rational normal scrolls, called $K3$ carpets. We compute exactly the cohomology of the twisted normal bundle of these $K3$ carpets, instead of computing coranks of Gaussian maps of the canonical curve sections. The key challenge is to analyze the coboundary map of the sequence relating the normal bundle of the $K3$ carpet to the normal bundle of the scroll. We give a deformation theoretic interpretation of this map. Given such a $K3$ carpet and its hyperplane section, which is a canonical ribbon, we show that the coboundary map corresponds to the obstruction to lifting a first order deformation of the underlying scroll fixing the underlying rational normal curve to a first order deformation of the $K3$ carpet fixing the canonical ribbon. To compute the obstruction, we use a result on extensions of non-split ribbons on any curve to a unique $K$-trivial carpet in a canonical way.
authors: with an appendix written jointly with Anand Deopurkar

papers.title: Finite groups with consistent subgroup lattices
papers.abstract: Motivated by the problem of Gragg and Kung on characterizing finite groups with consistent subgroup lattices, we investigate how the consistency of the subgroup lattice $L(G)$ constrains the structure of the underlying finite group $G$. To this end, we first establish several equivalent characterizations of consistency for lattices of finite length in terms of operation-preserving subposets and forbidden sublattices. More interestingly, for complete atomistic lattices of finite length, we introduce the consistency exchange property (CEP) for the canonical closure operator and show that consistency is equivalent to CEP, and that CEP is strictly weaker than the Steinitz-Mac Lane exchange property. We then apply this framework to semidirect products $G=V\rtimes_{\alpha} C_m$, where $V$ is an elementary abelian $p$-group, $m$ is square-free and $p\nmid m$. Writing $d=o(\alpha)$ and letting $C_\alpha=\langle\alpha\rangle$, we prove that $L(G)$ is consistent if and only if either $d=1$, or $d$ is prime and $V$ is isotypic as an $\mathbb F_pC_\alpha$-module. For prime $d$, this latter condition is equivalent both to the irreducibility of the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $\mathbb F_p$ and to $\mathbb F_p[\alpha]$ being a field. More generally, we verify that if $G=V\rtimes_\theta H$ where $H$ acts faithfully on $V$ and $p\nmid |H|$, then $L(G)$ is consistent if and only if either $H$ is trivial, or $H$ is cyclic of prime order and $V$ is isotypic as an $\mathbb F_pH$-module. We thus obtain a complete solution to the problem of Gragg and Kung for this class of coprime semidirect products.

papers.title: Finite Subgroups of Birational Automorphism Groups of Severi--Brauer Surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that a finite group acting birationally on a non-trivial Severi--Brauer surface $S$ over a field $\mathbb{K}$ of positive characteristic not equal to $3$ is isomorphic either to a subgroup of group of biregular automorphisms of $S_{\mathbb{K}^{per}}$ or to a subgroup of $\mu^3_3$, where $\mu_3$ is a cyclic group of order $3$ and $\mathbb{K}^{per}$ is the perfect closure of a field $\mathbb{K}$. Combined with results about classification of finite subgroups of the group of biregular automorphisms of $S$, this gives a classification of finite subgroups of the group of birational automorphisms of $S$.

papers.title: Finite torsion in Hodge--Witt cohomology groups
papers.abstract: For a bounded coherent complex of graded modules over the Raynaud ring $R$, we compare three descriptions of finite torsion: Ekedahl's pieces $A_f^2$ and $A_{\SSpart}^1$ of the biduality filtration, the nilpotent and semisimple parts of the torsion of the Illusie--Raynaud c\oe ur, and the corresponding parts of the finite torsion $t^1$ of Ekedahl's diagonal cohomology. We show that finite torsion in bidegree $(0,i+1)$ measures the failure of the $i$th flat Artin--Mazur formal group to be smooth; we deduce that all flat Artin--Mazur formal groups of a Mazur--Ogus variety are smooth. For a smooth projective surface, we identify the three possible dual pairs in terms of the $p$-primary torsion of the geometric N\'eron--Severi group and the local-local and local-\'etale parts of the finite Picard quotient.

papers.title: Foliated and compactly supported isotopies of tubular neighborhoods
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a foliation with a "singular" submanifold $\Sigma$ on a smooth manifold $A$ and $p:E \to \Sigma$ be a tubular neighborhood of $\Sigma$ in $A$. Under certain "scalability" assumptions on $\mathcal{F}$ near $\Sigma$, we prove that every leaf preserving diffeomorphism $h$ of $A$ is isotopic via a leaf preserving isotopy to a diffeomorphism which coincides with some vector bundle morphism of $E$ near $\Sigma$. This result is simultaneously a foliated, compactly supported and parametrized variant of a well known statement that every diffeomorphism $h$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ fixing the origin is isotopic to the linear isomorphism induced by its Jacobi matrix at $0$. Particular cases of such a "linearization theorem" allowed recently to compute homotopy types of leaf preserving diffeomorphism groups of polar Morse-Bott foliations on lens spaces and the twisted bundle $S^2\tilde{\times}S^1$.
  In general, that "linearization theorem" can be used to reduce the study of the homotopy type of the group of leaf preserving diffeomorphisms of $\mathcal{F}$ to an investigation of the following three groups (being independent in a certain sense): (a) diffeomorphism group of $\Sigma$, (b) the group of leaf preserving vector bundle isomorphisms of $E$, and (c) the group of leaf preserving diffeomorphisms of $A$ supported in $A\setminus \Sigma$, i.e. out of the "singularity" $\Sigma$.

papers.title: For Generalised Algebraic Theories, Two Sorts Are Enough
papers.abstract:
Generalised algebraic theories (GATs) allow multiple sorts indexed over each other. For example, the theories of categories or Martin-L{\"o}f type theories form GATs. Categories have two sorts, objects and morphisms, and the latter are double-indexed over the former. Martin-L{\"o}f type theory has four sorts: contexts, substitutions, types and terms. For example, types are indexed over contexts, and terms are indexed over both contexts and types. In this paper we show that any GAT can be reduced to a GAT with only two sorts, and there is a section-retraction correspondence (formally, a strict coreflection) between models of the original and the reduced GAT. In particular, any model of the original GAT can be turned into a model of the reduced (two-sorted) GAT and back, and this roundtrip is the identity.
  The reduced GAT is simpler than the original GAT in the following aspects: it does not have sort equalities; it does not have interleaved sorts and operations; if the original GAT did not have interleaved sorts and operations, then the reduced GAT won't have operations interleaved between different sorts. In a type-theoretic metatheory, the initial algebra of a GAT is called a quotient inductive-inductive type (QIIT). Our reduction provides a way to implement QIITs with sort equalities or interleaved constructors which are not allowed by Cubical Agda. An instance of our reduction is the well-known method of reducing mutual inductive types to a single indexed family. Our approach is semantic in that it does not rely on a syntactic description of GATs, but instead, on Uemura's bi-initial characterisation of the category of (finite) GATs in the 2-category of finitely complete categories with a chosen exponentiable morphism.

papers.title: Fourteenth-canonical birationality of threefolds with positive geometric genus
papers.abstract: We prove that the pluricanonical map of a complex projective threefold of general type with canonical singularities and positive geometric genus is birational in every degree at least fourteen. The bound is sharp.

papers.title: Frobenius and ozone automorphism groups of root of unity quantum cluster algebras
papers.abstract: Many important families of algebras $R$ in the areas of quantum groups, quantum topology and noncommutative algebra are root of unity quantum algebras, equipped with Frobenius centers $Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R) \subseteq Z(R)$ and quantum Frobenius maps ${\mathrm{Fr}} : R_{\mathrm{class}} \stackrel{\cong}{\longrightarrow} Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R)$. We explicitly classify the Frobenius automorphism groups ${\mathrm{Aut}}(R/Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R))$ and the ozone groups ${\mathrm{Oz}}(R):= {\mathrm{Aut}}(R/Z(R))$, and prove that all endomorphisms of $R$ fixing its Frobenius center $Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R)$ are automorphisms for all algebras $R$ that come from partial root of unity quantum cluster and upper quantum cluster algebras (which have been proved to encompass a vast majority of known quantum algebras). We prove three main theorems that give the above classification results from three different standpoints. As applications, we classify the Frobenius and ozone automorphism groups of all quantum function algebras of simple algebraic groups $G$ not of type $F_4$ or $E_8$ and all quantum unipotent cells at roots of unity for arbitrary symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebras.

papers.title: From Frobenius seeds to self-orthogonal modules over symmetric algebras
papers.abstract: We construct finite-dimensional symmetric algebras admitting nonprojective self-orthogonal modules from Frobenius algebras equipped with a module satisfying explicit stable and homological conditions. The resulting modules have complexity three, and their stable endomorphism algebras are isomorphic to the algebra of dual numbers over the ground field. The construction combines a variable input with a fixed auxiliary factor carrying the required twisting, and preserves the input through specified quotient and corner constructions. The proof combines derived induction, an obstruction to perfect factorization, and a cone construction over a Gorenstein triangular matrix algebra. For a symmetric algebra and a self-orthogonal generator, we describe the derived category of the opposite endomorphism algebra through a recollement with a two-term $2$-symmetric dg algebra. For our counterexamples, it is formal and quasi-isomorphic to an explicit four-dimensional dg algebra. Applications to cyclic coverings of a quantum exterior algebra yield connected examples with explicitly determined numbers of simple modules. The construction works over every field containing an element of infinite multiplicative order.

papers.title: From Hopf Algebras in Model Categories to Hopf Algebras in $\infty$-categories
papers.abstract: We show that algebra objects in model categories can be transferred to algebra objects in $\infty$-categories, without any cofibrancy or fibrancy assumptions on the algebra. We furthermore show under some mild extra assumptions that this correspondence extends to commutative bialgebras and to commutative Hopf algebras.

papers.title: Functorial Homological Mirror Symmetry for Acyclic Cluster Varieties
papers.abstract: We introduce the formalism of cluster models, a class of log Calabi-Yau varieties obtained from smooth quasi-affine toric varieties by iterated affine blowups along non-toric codimension 2 centers determined by a really full rank quiver. Cluster models include the truncated cluster varieties of Gross, Hacking, and Keel with respect to really full rank quivers, all really full rank acyclic cluster varieties, and all open toric subvarieties of $\mathbb{C}^n\times(\mathbb{C}^*)^m$. We then construct mirrors to cluster models via iterated Weinstein handle attachments to toric mirrors, so that the corresponding skeleta acquire compact pieces, and we prove homological mirror symmetry for all cluster models, compatibly with freezing, deleting, and contracting vertices of the quiver. This extends toric mirror symmetry and its naturalities beyond the cotangent bundle. In particular, we obtain homological mirror symmetry for all really full rank acyclic cluster varieties. We develop this package with a view towards conjectures of Marsh, Rietsch, and Williams about mirror symmetry for Grassmannians and closed positroid varieties. Motivated by these, we also conjecture that open positroid varieties are self-mirror. Assuming a natural ansatz, we prove this for a class of positroid varieties that includes nontrivial cells in every Grassmannian and all cells in finite-type Grassmannians. Towards this end we introduce a new combinatorial input, the notion of weak $k$-booleanness for permutations and braids.

papers.title: Generalizations of Igusa surfaces
papers.abstract: We give a criterion for the contracted product $E \times^G X$ to have a singular Picard scheme, where $E$ is an elliptic curve, $G \subset E$ is a finite subgroup scheme, and $X$ is a projective $G$-normal curve, in the sense of Brion. We show that every smooth projective surface with a singular Picard scheme and a positive-dimensional automorphism group scheme arises in this way. We also illustrate the criterion by constructing two new families of surfaces with singular Picard schemes, arising from $G$-normal curves $X$ for $G = \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $G = \boldsymbol{\alpha}_p$, respectively. As a special case of $G = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, we recover Igusa's classical example. Finally, we compute all infinitesimal group schemes which appear as $\operatorname{Pic}^0_S/(\operatorname{Pic}^0_S)_{\mathrm{red}}$ for all (quasi)-bielliptic surfaces $S$. This completes the description of the singular Picard schemes of smooth projective surfaces of Kodaira dimension zero.

papers.title: Generalized Divisors and Canonical Coarsening on Tame Deligne-Mumford Curves
papers.abstract: We study effective generalized divisors on reduced tame Deligne-Mumford curves over $\mathbb{C}$ satisfying $G_1$ and $S_2$. Canonical coarsening maps divisor ideals to coarse canonical lattices. We describe its fibres by exact intervals of equivariant lattices. For flat projective finite-quotient families of geometrically reduced Gorenstein curves over locally Noetherian bases, with finite constant groups and the stated relative-duality and base-change hypotheses, we construct projective invariant-Quot schemes for fixed canonical lattices with finite flat quotients and prescribed quotient representations. A nontrivial marked deformation preserves the coarse ring, normalization, conductor and entire fixed canonical fibre, while a length-four isotypic jet detects its parameter. We compute the full normalization and conductor correction after support restriction on an explicit rank-three chart. As a module, the correction splits into one surface and two line canonical modules, with a common grading shift. The corresponding square-zero algebra extension is nonsplit. The full source-support pair is compared through second order. Exact computational certificates accompany the proofs.

papers.title: Generalized near-group tensor categories
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a finite tensor category with exactly one isomorphism class of simple objects which are non-invertible.
  Semisimple tensor categories $\mathcal{D}$ with this property are called near-group categories, and have been studied by Evans, Gannon, Siehler and others. In this paper, we study such categories in the non-semisimple setting, with the additional assumption that the non-invertible simple object is projective. Specifically, we consider the case when $\mathcal{D}$ admits a fiber functor and has a unique semisimple abelian block (in the general case that $\D$ is not semisimple). We describe the structure of such categories and their corresponding Hopf algebras, and construct examples of such categories with a cyclic Picard group.
