We obtain additional results when the Frobenius-Perron dimension of the unique non-invertible simple object is a prime number.

papers.title: Gersten resolutions for logarithmic forms
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth variety over a field $k$ of characteristic 0. We show that (two versions of) the Zariski sheaves of regular $k$-linear logarithmic differential forms on $X$ (in the most na\"{\i}ve sense, i.e. sums of products of logarithmic differentials) have Gersten property (and therefore coincide). It turns out that the values of these sheaves are free abelian groups. As a consequence, for any integer $n>0$, these sheaves modulo $n$ also have Gersten property. The proof is an elementary application of the Voevodsky's $(-1)$-machinery and consists of assembling several well-known results.

papers.title: Global-dimension spectra of gentle algebras
papers.abstract:
We classify the connected finite-dimensional gentle algebras of finite global dimension whose global-dimension spectra under derived equivalence are not intervals of integers. These are precisely the algebras with AAG invariant $[(2,4g)]$, where $g\geq2$, whose canonical line field is induced by a nowhere-vanishing vector field. Their spectrum is $\{2g,2g+2,\ldots,4g\}$. For each $g\geq2$, there are exactly two such derived-equivalence classes, distinguished by their Arf invariant.
  The geometric foundation is a realisation theorem for prescribed polygon weights in arbitrary genus. For an AAG invariant $[(m_i,n_i)]_{i=1}^b$ arising from such an algebra, the global dimensions attained in its AAG fibre form the integer interval $[\max_i\lceil n_i/m_i\rceil,\max_i n_i]$. By controlling the complete line-field invariant through local ribbon-graph constructions, we determine the spectrum in every derived-equivalence class.

papers.title: Graded String Diagrams with Applications in Probabilistic Reasoning
papers.abstract:
We introduce string diagrams for graded symmetric monoidal categories. Our approach includes a definition of graded monoidal theory and the corresponding freely generated syntactic category. The para construction on monoidal actegories is a motivating example for our framework, and we show how an axiomatic presentation of the resulting category $\mathbf{Para}(\mathbb{G},\mathbf{C})$ may be modularly obtained from presentations for $\mathbb{G}$ and $\mathbf{C}$. We demonstrate three different applications of our diagrammatic language under the same theme: probabilistic reasoning.
  First, we show how to axiomatise a variant of the graded category $\mathbf{ImP}$, recently introduced by Liell-Cock and Staton to model imprecise probability. This culminates in a representation, as string diagrams with grading wires, of programs with primitives for nondeterministic and probabilistic choices and conditioning. Second, we exploit our modular presentation result to provide a new proof for a presentation of $\mathbf{Gauss}$, the category of Gaussian stochastic maps. Third, we use grading wires to represent causal interventions on Bayesian networks.

papers.title: Haagerup symmetry in a rank-six lattice conformal field theory
papers.abstract: Let $U$ be a positive strongly rational vertex operator algebra of central charge eight with $\mathrm{Rep}(U) \cong Z(\cal H_3)$. We show that its Cartan Heisenberg commutant $\Omega$ embeds conformally into a lattice algebra $V_K$, where $K$ has rank six, determinant $39$ and root system $A_2\oplus A_2\oplus A_1$. The diagonal theory of $V_K$ has a unique vacuum and carries each of the three Haagerup fusion categories through three nonconjugate embeddings of $\Omega$. We show that, up to isomorphism fixing $\Omega$, there are exactly five conformal extensions of $\Omega$ with positive strongly rational target and global representation-category dimension $39$, and that their images in $V_K$ form four conjugacy classes. We also determine the common invariant relevant spectrum of the three canonical actions, their normalized cubic constants and their invariant genus-zero field algebra. We work in the TFT framework of rational full conformal field theory.

papers.title: Hecke curves in Frobenius strata of moduli space of rank 2 vector bundles
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field with characteristic $2$, and let $X$ be a smooth projective algebraic curve of genus $g \geqslant 2$ over $k$. Let $\mathcal{M}^s_X(2,\mathcal{L})$ be the moduli space of rank $2$ stable vector bundles with determinant $\mathcal{L}$ on $X$. The Frobenius stratification measures the instability of bundles in $\mathcal{M}^s_X(r,\mathcal{L})$ under pullback by the Frobenius map. We show that there exists a Frobenius stratum in $\mathcal{M}^s_X(2,\mathcal{L})$ which is covered by Hecke curves.

papers.title: Highest weight category structures on $rep(B)$ and full exceptional collections on generalized flag varieties over $\mathbb Z$
papers.abstract: Given a split simply connected semi-simple algebraic group scheme $\mathbb G$ over $\mathbb Z$, a split maximaltorus $\mathbb T$ in $\mathbb G$and a parabolic subgroup scheme $\mathbb P\supset \mathbb T$, this paper constructs semi-orthogonal decompositions of the bounded derived category $D^b(rep(\mathbb P))$ of noetherian representations of $\mathbb P$ with each semi-orthogonal component being equivalent to the bounded derived category $D^b(rep(\mathbb G))$ of noetherian representations of $\mathbb G$. The semi-orthogonal components of those decompositions are stable under the monoidal action of $D^b(rep(\mathbb G))$ on $D^b(rep(\mathbb P))$. The decompositions depend on an arbitrarily chosen total order on the Weyl group that refines the Bruhat order. The semi-orthogonal decompositions are also compatible with the Bruhat order on cosets of the Weyl group of $\mathbb P$ in the Weyl group of $\mathbb G$. Their construction builds upon the foundational results on $\mathbb B$-modules from the works of Mathieu, Polo, and van der Kallen, and upon properties of the Steinberg basis of the $\mathbb T$-equivariant $K$-theory of $\mathbb G/\mathbb B$. As a corollary, we obtain full exceptional collections in the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on generalized flag schemes $\mathbb G/\mathbb P$ over $\mathbb Z$.

papers.title: Holographic entropy inequalities without unscaled contraction proofs
papers.abstract: We show that a valid holographic entropy inequality can lack a proof by contraction until all its coefficients are multiplied by a common integer, even when it is balanced, that is, every party has the same total coefficient on both sides, or superbalanced, that is, this remains true after any party is exchanged with the purifier. Every facet of the holographic entropy cone other than subadditivity is superbalanced. A proof by contraction is a map between Boolean cubes that respects the terms in which each party occurs and does not increase weighted Hamming distances. A balanced seven-party inequality and a superbalanced six-party inequality fail at a single point of the cube. Six of their right-hand side terms correspond to the edges of two disjoint triangles of parties, and at that point an unscaled map would have to choose three of these edges that together touch all six vertices, which is impossible. The seven-party one has a proof after doubling. Superbalanced eight- and seven-party inequalities have no unscaled proof even on their realizable domains, the subsets of the cube on which a map already proves validity, and they keep this property when instances of the monogamy of mutual information are subtracted in five successive steps. Splitting further into valid inequalities leads to a superbalanced facet $F_7$ of the seven-party cone that we did not find in the literature. It has unscaled maps on its realizable domain, all of which break its symmetry. For star inequalities, whose left-hand side contains only single-party entropies, the least scaling is the least $k$ for which an explicit polytope contains a point with coordinates in $\frac1k\mathbb{Z}$. From the weighing matrices of Alon and V\~u we obtain valid $N$-party star inequalities whose least scaling exceeds $N^{(1/4-\varepsilon)N}$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and large $N$, while every finite least scaling of an $N$-party star inequality is below $N^{N/2}$. Non-existence rests on DRAT proofs, validity on exact rational maps or identities, and the facet property on $126$ explicit graph models, except for the star inequalities of arbitrary size, whose results rest on written proofs.

papers.title: Homology and higher-order intermediate categories for proper abelian subcategories
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an extension-closed proper abelian subcategory of a triangulated category $\mathcal{C}$, and put $\mathcal{D}_\ell=\Sigma^\ell\mathcal{A}*\cdots*\mathcal{A}$ for $\ell\geq 1$. Assuming that $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{C}}(\Sigma^p\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A})=0$ for $1\leq p\leq\ell+1$, we construct homology functors $H_i:\mathcal{D}_\ell\to\mathcal{A}$ for $0\leq i\leq\ell$ and prove that triangles in $\mathcal{D}_\ell$ induce natural long exact sequences in $\mathcal{A}$. If $\mathcal{C}$ is Krull--Schmidt, we introduce compatible sequences of subcategories of $\mathcal{A}$ and use them to classify the homology-determined subcategories $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathcal{D}_\ell$ that are closed under extensions and direct summands.

papers.title: Images of Multilinear Polynomials with a Standard-Polynomial Unit Specialization
papers.abstract: For $r=3,4,5$, consider an ordinary multilinear polynomial $f(Y,X_1,\ldots,X_{2r})$ whose specialization at $Y=I$ is a nonzero scalar multiple of the standard polynomial $s_{2r}$. Over an algebraically closed field $K$ of characteristic zero, we prove that for every $n\ge r+1$ the set of its individual values on $M_n(K)$ is $\mathfrak{sl}n(K)$ if its trace vanishes identically, and $M_n(K)$ otherwise. This includes arbitrary proper perturbations of $s_7,s_9,s{11}$. The proof combines exact standard-polynomial core constructions, additive size transfer, and a mixed-frame compatibility lemma with a local lifting criterion of Pan.

papers.title: Improved scaling in the metric cotype inequality
papers.abstract: Let \(2\le q<\infty\). It is proved that every Banach space with Rademacher cotype \(q\) satisfies the metric cotype \(q\) inequality with scaling parameter \(m=O(n^{1/2+1/q})\). The improved bound on the scaling is achieved by reducing the metric cotype problem to a smoothing and approximation criterion on the continuous torus. For a single unconditional kernel, the criterion is controlled by its mean \(\ell_\infty\) radius and its variation in the main diagonal direction. The construction fits the universal smoothing and approximation scheme of Giladi, Mendel, and Naor. The proofs were generated by GPT~6 Astra with the help of the author.

papers.title: Inhomogeneous deformations of $\mathfrak{osp}(N|2n)$: triviality for any number of odd parameters
papers.abstract: We treat a symmetrized mixed-oscillator deformation family of the orthosymplectic Lie superalgebras $\mathfrak{osp}(N|2n)$, $N,n\geq1$, with even mixed coefficients $\beta_{u,i}$ and one odd square-zero parameter. We derive the deformed bracket from an oscillator realization, show that its coefficient is determined by the realization, and exhibit an explicit odd primitive, normalized by its vanishing on $\mathfrak{sp}(2n)$. Every odd primitive differs from it by a unique inner derivation. For $N=1$ this is the case $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2n)$ treated earlier. With multiple odd parameters the deformed bracket is the sum of the single-parameter deformations and is again trivial. The trivialization, however, is not additive: it is the product of the single-parameter trivializations followed by a nonsymplectic change of the bosonic generators. The main results are formalized in Lean~4, with the algebras constructed by generators and relations; what is not formalized is stated in the appendix.

papers.title: Internal structures in the category of right-preordered groups
papers.abstract: We give explicit axioms for the algebraic theory of the quasivarieties of right-preordered groups and preordered groups. We then look at lattices of effective equivalence relations, which turn out to be similar to the lattices of equivalence relations in the category of groups. Once this is established, we study internal structures in the category of right-preordered groups. We start with some general results and then prove the S-protomodularity of the category of right-preordered groups, when considering the class S of Schreier split epimorphisms. Following this, we investigate further and prove that the category of right-preordered groups turns out to be action representable when we restrict our attention to split epimorphisms in S. Relatively to this class of split epimorphisms, we define the notion of S-precrossed modules, and then of S-crossed modules; that correspond exactly to Schreier internal reflexive graphs and Schreier internal categories, respectively. Lastly, we characterize groupoids among Schreier internal categories and give some examples.

papers.title: Invariant operations on vector fields on the line are Lie polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove that all $W_1$-equivariant multilinear operations on the Witt Lie algebra $W_1$ are Lie polynomials. We study this question in terms of Wronskian Lie brackets and Novikov products, which are abstractions of the Lie bracket $[a,b]:=ab'-ba'$ and the nonassociative product $a\circ b=ab'$ one can define on a commutative differential algebra. In terms of these notions, our main result asserts that the operad of Wronskian Lie algebras is isomorphic to the operad of equivariant multilinear operations on~$W_1$; we also prove a parallel result for the operad of Novikov algebras, characterizing it as the operad of affine equivariant multilinear operations on $W_1$. Two immediate consequences of our work are a characterization of Lie polynomials in free Novikov algebras and a computation of the degree zero homology of the operadic twisting of the Novikov operad. Finally, while it is known that over a field of zero characteristic, a Novikov algebra embeds into its differential envelope, we show that the same is not necessarily true for Wronskian Lie algebras.

papers.title: Irreducibility of Verma modules for symmetrizable Kac-Moody superalgebras
papers.abstract: We establish a criterion for the irreducibility of Verma modules over symmetrizable Kac--Moody superalgebras. Our main tool is the Weyl-Kac denominator identity.

papers.title: Irreducible Representations as Local Maxima of a Matrix-Coefficient Functional
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional unitary representation of a finite group $G$ and, for unit vectors $v$, let $\Phi(v)$ be the mean of $|\langle v,gv\rangle|^2$ over $g\in G$. We show that $v$ is a local maximum of $\Phi$ if and only if the subrepresentation generated by $v$ is irreducible. Thus local maximization of $\Phi$ extracts irreducible subrepresentations of $V$ directly, with no character or isotypic projection specified in advance. The proof is elementary: Schur averaging reduces it to a singular-value calculation. The values and dimensions of the connected components of the local-maximum set determine the degrees and multiplicities of the irreducible constituents, and for $H\leq G$ the intersections of the $G$- and $H$-local-maximal loci encode branching multiplicities. We also determine the critical landscape and give a normalized gradient iteration whose generic limit generates an irreducible subrepresentation.

papers.title: Kato's Ramification filtration via de Rham-Witt complex and applications
papers.abstract:
Given an $F$-finite regular scheme $X$ of positive characteristic and a
  simple normal crossing divisor $E$ on $X$,
  we introduce a filtration on the de Rham--Witt
  complex $W_m\Omega^\bullet_{X\setminus E}$. When $X$ is the spectrum of a
  henselian discrete valuation ring $A$ with quotient field $K$,
  this extends the classical filtration on
  $W_m(K)$ due to Brylinski. We show that Kato's ramification filtration on $H^q_\et(X \setminus E, {\Q}/{\Z}(q-1))$ for $q \ge 1$ admits an explicit
  description in terms of the above filtration on the de Rham--Witt complex
  of $X \setminus E$. When $q =1$, this specializes to the results of Kato and
  Kerz--Saito.
  As applications, we construct a generalized version of Kato's refined Swan conductor
  for regular schemes, prove Lefschetz theorems for Kato's ramification filtrations
  for smooth projective varieties over $F$-finite fields, and prove
  Lefschetz and vanishing theorems for the Brauer group.

papers.title: Lipschitz inner rates of normal surface singularities
papers.abstract: In this article, we connect the local Lipschitz geometry of a normal surface singularity with a rational homology sphere link to the analytic semigroup $S_{an}(\tilde{X})$ associated with a convenient resolution. Under certain restriction, we provide an explicit computational characterization of the Lipschitz rate $q_v$ associated with an irreducible exceptional curve $E_v$ in terms of the semigroup. We also show that removing the restriction we get examples when $q_v$ cannot be determined from the semigroup. Interestingly enough, this phenomenon already happens for rational singularities. Indeed, we exemplify that the inner rates of rational singularities are not topological.

papers.title: Lusztig's sharp bound for Hecke algebras
papers.abstract: We prove Lusztig's sharp boundedness conjecture for Hecke algebras of finite-rank Coxeter systems with positive integer-valued weight functions.

papers.title: Magnitude homology of real hyperplane arrangements
papers.abstract: We define and study the magnitude and magnitude homology of real hyperplane arrangements by regarding their tope graphs as metric spaces. Since magnitude is a refinement of the cardinality, this may be viewed as a natural generalization of the classical problem of counting the chambers of an arrangement. Our central result is a structure theorem asserting that the magnitude and magnitude homology of an arrangement decompose into contributions indexed by its faces. In particular, the magnitude is determined by the intersection lattice of the arrangement. We also observe several interesting phenomena, including a characterization of Boolean arrangements in terms of diagonality and a reciprocity theorem reminiscent of Ehrhart--Macdonald reciprocity. Finally, based on explicit computations, we conjecture that the magnitude homology of an arrangement is torsion-free and determined by its intersection lattice.

papers.title: Making the coprimality convention explicit in a mean value theorem of Halupczok for the ternary Goldbach problem
papers.abstract: Theorem 1.2 of Halupczok (2013) is a Bombieri-Vinogradov type mean value theorem for the ternary Goldbach problem with one prime in an arithmetic progression and two primes in short intervals. Her proof works with residue classes $a \bmod q$ coprime to the modulus, as stated on p. 344 of her paper, and this convention needs to be written explicitly into the statement because the printed product and the prime sum differ at $a = q = 3$, where the prime sum is $0$ for $X_1 > 3$ while the printed product is at least $9/16$ for odd $n$. We give two closely related explicit formulations, Formulation A and Formulation B, show that Formulation A implies Formulation B, and prove both assuming two cited inputs, Hypothesis H1 and Hypothesis H2, or alternatively Theorems 2.1 and 2.3 of her paper, which follow from these two inputs. Here Hypothesis H1 is a uniform reading of a printed remark of Perelli, Pintz and Salerno, supported by a reading of the proof, and Hypothesis H2 is assembled from displays of Perelli and Pintz and is not a numbered statement. The supplement of Theorem 1.2 with a maximum over $a$ is not covered. The later results of Halupczok's paper use only coprime residue classes and are unaffected. The main results of this note have been checked by computer.

papers.title: Metric Multiview Geometry---a Catalogue in Low Dimensions
papers.abstract: We systematically compile an exhaustive catalogue of multiview varieties and anchored multiview varieties arising from projections of points, lines, and planes in 1, 2, and 3-dimensional projective spaces. We say that two such varieties are ED-equivalent if there is a linear isomorphism between them that preserves ED-critical points. This gives rise to fourteen representatives, at most two of which are equivalent, and we determine various properties---dimension, set-theoretic equations, and multidegrees---for all varieties featured in our catalogue. In the case of points, we also present a complementary study of resectioning varieties and their singular loci. Finally, we propose conjectures for the Euclidean distance degrees of all varieties appearing in our comprehensive compilation.

papers.title: Metric nefness of direct image sheaves under weakly semi-stable K\"ahler morphisms
papers.abstract: We investigate the nefness of the direct image sheaves of relative adjoint bundles under weakly semi-stable K\"ahler morphisms between complex spaces. We show that the direct image sheaves are locally free and that their tautological line bundles are metrically nef, strengthening the previously known results on torsion-freeness and certain weak positivity.

papers.title: Monomial Immanants of Totally Nonnegative Matrices
papers.abstract: We prove that every monomial immanant is nonnegative on the totally nonnegative real matrices, establishing a conjecture of Stembridge. We identify the corresponding normalized symmetric function of annular holonomy with a single cluster theta function.

papers.title: Monotonicity of Erdős sums
papers.abstract: For $k \geq 1$ let $f_k = \sum_{\Omega(n)=k} 1/(n\log n)$, where $\Omega$ counts prime factors with multiplicity, and let $g_k$ be the same sum restricted to odd $n$. Lichtman showed that $f_k \to 1$, with a global minimum at $k=6$, and Gorodetsky, Lichtman and Wong that $f_k = 1 - 2^{-k}(a_1 k^2 + O(k \log(k+1)))$. We prove that $f_k < f_{k+1}$ for every $k \geq 6$, and that $g_k > g_{k+1}$ for every $k \geq 1$. The two statements come from one analytic distinction. Writing $\sum_k P_k(s) z^k = \zeta(s)^z H(s,z)$, at $s=1$ the point $z=2$ lies on the first singular circle of $H$, and strictly inside the first singular circle of the product with the prime $2$ removed. We show that this distinction decides the direction in general. If the complement of a set of primes $\mathcal{P}$ is thin and its least element is at least $3$, the corresponding sums eventually decrease, so the second theorem is one case of a general phenomenon. The inequalities used at the last step of the first theorem are certified by interval arithmetic.

papers.title: Motivic generating functions and $L$-derivatives of cohomological automorphic representations
papers.abstract: Forty years ago, Gross and Zagier proved a remarkable formula computing the central derivative of the Rankin--Selberg $L$-function of a cusp form $f$ of weight $2$ and a character of the class group of an imaginary quadratic field, satisfying the so-called Heegner condition, and deduce that the nonvanishing of the central derivative implies the nonvanishing of the corresponding Mordell--Weil rank. This formula was later generalized in various contexts and degrees, for example, by S. Zhang for $f$ of higher even weights; and by Yuan--Zhang--Zhang for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form of parallel weight $2$ over an arbitrary totally real field $F$ and $\chi$ a Dirichlet character of an arbitrary CM extension $E/F$, allowing arbitrary ramification. In this article, we prove a Gross--Zagier type formula in the context of doubling method, for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form over $F$ and $\chi$ a Hecke character of $E$ of general weights under a balancing condition, again allowing arbitrary ramification. Indeed, we even formulate a general conjecture which we call the motivic arithmetic inner product formula, for cohomological automorphic representations of $\mathrm{GL}_{2r}$ over $E$ of hermitian type of balanced weights.

papers.title: Multivariate Pellarin $L$-values on algebraic curves
papers.abstract: We establish a generating trace formula for multicharacter ideal-type $L$-values associated with rank-one Drinfeld modules. For a sign-normalized Hayes module with free period lattice, the formula realizes the $L$-values at weights $n\equiv s\pmod{q^{\deg_\infty}-1}$ as a trace over the ordinary Hilbert class field. We further characterize the polynomials in the exponential variable $X$ arising in multicharacter lattice generating identities over arbitrary function rings. Their coefficients are given explicitly via the shtuka basis, which gives concrete control over their supports and degrees. This completely settles an open problem of Pellarin and Perkins: these polynomials are all constant if and only if $s<2q$. The results on coefficients apply to curves of arbitrary genus, infinite places of arbitrary degree, and nonprincipal period lattices.

papers.title: Mutation of Theta Functions
papers.abstract: We give an account of mutation of theta functions in cluster scattering diagrams, starting with a notion of mutation that is related to, but different from, the notion of mutation defined by Gross, Hacking, Keel, and Kontsevich.This different approach to mutation leads to several applications. Three of the applications simplify the process of computing structure constants for multiplication of theta functions, and these are used in another paper on cluster scattering diagrams of affine type. Notable in these three applications is the appearance of mutation symmetries and dominance regions. The other two applications have to do with pointed reduced bases, a variation on the pointed bases of Fan Qin. We give a characterization of pointed reduced bases analogous to Qin's characterization of pointed bases. All of these applications take place in a version of Gross, Hacking, Keel, and Kontsevich's canonical algebra that can be constructed for an arbitrary exchange matrix.

papers.title: NC-smooth thickenings and Jacobians
papers.abstract: We prove that a bounded complex of coherent sheaves on an abelian variety A, whose Fourier-Mukai transform has support of dimension at most 1, extends to a perfect complex on the standard NC-smooth thickening of A and on the deformation quantization of any constant Poisson bracket on A. We discuss a related conjectural characterization of Jacobians in terms of NC-smooth thickenings.

papers.title: New families of maximal curves not covered by the Hermitian curve and their cyclic automorphism groups
papers.abstract: For every prime power $q>2$, integer $n\ge2$ and $1\le r\le 2n-1$, we construct an $\mathbb F_{q^{2n}}$-maximal curve $T_{q,n,r}$ with Kummer equation \[ z^{q^n+1}=\eta^{-R}y(1-y^{q-1})^R, \qquad \frac{q^r-1}{q-1},\] where $\eta\in\mathbb F_{q^{2n}}^*$ satisfies $\eta^{q^n}=-\eta$. For fixed $q,n$, these are cyclic covers of the projective line over a single field, indexed by the integer $r$. Writing $\delta=\gcd(q^n+1,R)$, we prove that the genus is $(q-1)(q^n+1-\delta)/2$ and that $T_{q,n,r}$ is covered by the Hermitian curve $\mathcal H_{q^n}$ over an algebraic closure if and only if $\min(r,2n-r)$ divides $n$. For $1<r<n$ and $\delta=1$, the full automorphism group is cyclic of order $(q-1)(q^n+1)$, and distinct values of $r$ give curves that are nonisomorphic over an algebraic closure despite having the same genus and full automorphism group. We also give explicit equations and genera for all their Galois subfields. When $n\ge 4$ is a power of two, this produces families over a fixed field whose members are not covered by $\mathcal H_{q^n}$.

papers.title: New nonabelian Hodge graphs from twisted irregular connections
papers.abstract: It is known that any meromorphic connection on the Riemann sphere determines a finite diagram (a generalised graph, possibly with negative edge multiplicities), which is invariant under the Fourier-Laplace transform. If the connection has regular singularities at finite distance and an untwisted irregular singularity at infinity, the diagram is a supernova graph, and the quiver modularity theorem of Boalch/Hiroe-Yamakawa shows that the corresponding nonabelian Hodge moduli space contains the Nakajima quiver variety of the graph as an open subset. In this note, motivated by the question of classifying these nonabelian Hodge diagrams, we obtain a necessary condition satisfied by all (core) nonabelian Hodge diagrams, involving ultrametric inequalities. We use this to investigate the class of such diagrams that are graphs (without edge-loops nor negative multiplicities), as well as certain special classes of nonabelian Hodge graphs: we show that there exist nonabelian Hodge graphs beyond the setting of the quiver modularity theorem, and obtain characterisations of fission graphs and of simply-laced nonabelian Hodge graphs.

papers.title: No arrivals: complete periodicity and degenerate orbits in rational right triangles
papers.abstract: Boshernitzan conjectured in 1992 that in a rational right or isosceles triangle every direction of an explicit finite set is purely periodic: every billiard orbit in it that avoids the vertices is periodic. For a right triangle with acute angle $P\pi/2Q$ in lowest terms the set is two classes of directions, each containing the perpendicular to a side, and the conjecture says that both are completely periodic. It fails at one known right triangle, $(4/15, 7/30, 1/2)\pi$. We prove it, when $\min(P, Q - P) \geq 2$, whenever $P + 2$ and $P - 2$ are both prime to $Q$, a set of density about $0.62$, and whenever $Q$ has at most one odd prime factor, with a computer-assisted check of finitely many cases; and, through the fold, for the corresponding isosceles triangles. Everything turns on one object, an orbit from a vertex to a vertex that never strikes a side at a right angle: if there is none, both classes are completely periodic, and at odd $P$ the retracing band of a companion paper exists. Such an orbit satisfies an identity among roots of unity whose coefficients have signs fixed by the geometry, and Galois conjugation — or, at a single odd prime, a slowest-rotation argument — makes it impossible. When neither $P + 2$ nor $P - 2$ is a unit modulo $Q$, no argument from these inputs can succeed, and the counterexample lies there. A second method reads the poles of a minimal component as a word of a binary code attached to $Q$; it reaches further composite $Q$ and, with interval arithmetic, the triangles $(4, Q - 4, Q)$ at every $Q \equiv 3 \pmod{4}$. Beyond right triangles we prove, with computer assistance, that Boshernitzan's Conjecture 2.2(a) fails for infinitely many triangles.

papers.title: Non-computable derivatives of the fractional-part autocorrelation
papers.abstract: We describe a natural new example of non-computability in analysis. Namely, the multiplicative autocorrelation of the fractional-part function, \[ A(x)=\int_0^\infty \{t\}\{xt\}\,\frac{dt}{t^2}, \] is computable and differentiable almost everywhere, but its finite derivative can be non-computable even for a computable $x$. We derive these results from an adaptation of our earlier work on computability of Brjuno-like functions.

papers.title: Noncommutative Hourglasses I: On the Classification of Q-Fano 3-Folds of Gorenstein Index 2 via Derived Categories
papers.abstract: In previous work, Takagi used the methods of solving the Sarkisov links by calculating the corresponding Diophantine equations and the construction of key varieties to give all possible classifications and some implementations of a class $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano 3-fold with Fano index 1/2 and at worst $(1, 1, 1)/2$ or QODP singularities. Firstly, we use a method different from Kawamata's work to give the derived category formulas for general weighted blow-up and Kawamata weighted blow-up. On this basis, we study the changing behavior of the derived category of Takagi's varieties under Sarkisov links. Finally, by studying non-commutative projections, we give exceptional collections on the derived category of Takagi's varieties and their corresponding geometric meanings.

papers.title: Nonexistence of DSRGs with ten parameter sets: the rank of A − θI versus a submatrix prescribed at a vertex
papers.abstract: For a directed strongly regular graph (DSRG), the parameters determine rank(A − θI) at nontrivial eigenvalues θ. For small λ or t = λ + 1 they almost determine a piece of this matrix at a vertex: a piece needing more rank excludes the graph, and a small margin leaves finitely many cases. We exclude (50, 11, 7, 0, 3), (68, 13, 7, 0, 3), (100, 16, 7, 0, 3), (108, 19, 9, 0, 4), (48, 9, 5, 0, 2), (55, 16, 12, 1, 6), (66, 10, 5, 4, 1) and (91, 12, 6, 5, 1), open in Hobart and Brouwer's table, and their complements. Counting twin classes reproves (96, 15, 10, 9, 1) and (28, 6, 3, 2, 1): for the first, rank replaces one counting bound; for the second, it is unused. Lean 4 with Mathlib proves nine exclusions; for (28, 6, 3, 2, 1) its kernel also checks a SAT certificate. (48, 9, 5, 0, 2) ends with a search by two separately written programs, the second certified by CaDiCaL unsatisfiability proofs checked by drat-trim.

papers.title: Nonuniqueness of site percolation on nonamenable quasi-transitive graphs
papers.abstract: Benjamini and Schramm conjectured in 1996 that site percolation on every nonamenable quasi-transitive graph has $p_c<p_u$. We prove this in Hutchcroft's operator form: for Bernoulli site percolation on every connected, locally finite, nonamenable quasi-transitive graph, the critical two-point operator is bounded on $\ell^2$, $p_c<p_{2\to2}\le p_u$, and in the standard monotone coupling infinitely many infinite clusters coexist at every parameter of a nondegenerate interval. Since bond percolation is site percolation on the line graph, this contains OpenAI's recent bond theorem. For unimodular automorphism groups we adapt OpenAI's proof: cut vertices replace bridges, a pruning lemma handles retained contact vertices, a rejection step controls the junctions created by opening a vertex, and pivotal corridors become induced paths. For nonunimodular groups we extend Tran and Nguyen's site argument from vertex-transitive to quasi-transitive graphs.

papers.title: Odd/Odd Records for a Relative Approximation Error: Three Quadratic Classifications and an Exact Certificate
papers.abstract: For a quadratic irrational α > 1 and positive odd integers m, k, set H = mα + k and ε = |mα − k|/(mα + k). A state (m, k) is a strict chronological record if ε is smaller than at every admissible state of smaller H. We classify the strict records completely for α = φ, α = 1 + √3 and α = √3. In each case they are a finite explicit union of orbits of a single unimodular matrix, with signed defect cycles (−1, +1, −5), (−3, +1, −11) and (−2) respectively. The proofs rest on two exact identities that make ε a function of the defect N and the conjugate factor η alone, on a norm cutoff |N| ≤ 18, 204, 27 derived from heights, and on a finite exact certificate that decides every remaining comparison. Two phenomena require care and are isolated: at φ the competition between the Fibonacci and Lucas ladders is a genuine tie at leading order, decided by an integer identity N_B = −5N_A; and at √3 a companion family has exactly equal error at larger height, so it is excluded by equality rather than by loss. The results resolve two conjectures of the author's earlier note and correct one assertion there. Nothing here is formally verified or refereed, and the uniform generalisation is left open.

papers.title: On $\mathrm{HH}^1$ of blocks of finite simple group algebras
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a sporadic simple group, $k$ a field of positive characteristic and assume $B$ is a block of $kG$ with non-trivial defect. In this paper we prove the first Hochschild cohomology group $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)$ is non-vanishing. Furthermore, we prove that for every wild block with abelian defect of a sporadic simple group, we have that $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)$ is a solvable Lie algebra of derived length two, with non-zero maximal toral rank.

papers.title: On a basepoint issue in the tempered dual of $p$-adic $SL(n)$
papers.abstract:
Let $F$ be a non-archimedean local field of characteristic zero. Let $M$ be a Levi subgroup of $G = \mathrm{SL}(n,F)$. Consider the action on the discrete series of $M$ of the group of unitary unramified characters of $M$ (where a character acts by twisting). Given an orbit $\mathcal{O}$ for that action, let $W_\mathcal{O}$ be the global stabilizer of $\mathcal{O}$ in the Weyl group of $M$. We construct families of orbits $\mathcal{O}$ for which the action of $W_\mathcal{O}$ has no fixed point.
  More precisely, let $n \geq 8$ be an integer that is not prime and not equal to $9$. We attach families of orbits without fixed points to any divisor $m \geq 2$ of $n$ such that $m \;| \; q-1$ where $q$ is the order of the residue field of $F$. The Levi subgroup $M \subset G$ for the corresponding families has $m$ blocks of size $k\geq 2$ and $2$ blocks of size $m$. The core of the paper is the construction of superculpidal representations of $\mathrm{GL}(m,F)$ and $\mathrm{GL}(k,F)$ satisfying some conditions that we require to construct the families of orbits $\mathcal{O}$ that we expects.
  In addition, we study the fixed point problem for the dimensions $n$ that we excluded above, i.e., prime or small dimensions. We prove that there is always a fixed point under the action of $W_\mathcal{O}$ in those cases.

papers.title: On deformations of foliated complex analytic structures IV-1: Obstructed and unobstructed foliated deformations
papers.abstract: We study obstructions of deformations of foliated complex analytic structures. We describe obstructions in terms of Cech resolutions. From foliated complex analytic families in Part I and unfolded complex analytic families in Part III, we deduce the integrability conditions. We identify infinitesimal deformations and obstructions in terms of Dolbeault resolutions or Dolbeault type bicomplexes from the integrability conditions. Then we describe the correspondences of infinitesimal deformations and obstructions between Cech resolutions, and Dolbeault resolutions or Dolbeault type bicomplexes.

papers.title: On Fourier and Hadamard matrices of prime order
papers.abstract: We study how much of the Fourier matrix $F_p$ is needed to recognize it among complex Hadamard matrices of prime order $p$. For regular or Butson matrices, taking the $p$th power of each entry gives either a Hadamard matrix or a matrix of rank one. For every odd prime, the block of $F_p$ on the rows and columns indexed by the nonzero squares determines $F_p$ up to equivalence in both classes. At level $p$, a symmetry with cycle lengths $1,(p-1)/2,(p-1)/2$ on each side also characterizes $F_p$ at every odd prime through $109$.

papers.title: On naturality of cohomological support for small quantum groups
papers.abstract: We apply the theory of hypersurface support by Negron and Pevtsova to prove the naturality of cohomological support of the small quantum Borel groups, with respect to restriction to Levi subalgebras. This in turn implies naturality of cohomological support of the small quantum groups for modules that lift to Lusztig's big quantum group, for instance tilting modules. This allows us to make the recent conditional classification of tensor ideals of abelian type in the category of such tilting modules unconditional.

papers.title: On Proximity Subgroups of Groups
papers.abstract:
By a $	extit{proximity subgroup}$ of a group $G$ we mean a norm $
u$ on $G$ valued in a complete lattice $L$ equipped with a binary sum (an additive counterpart of a multiplicative structure). The idea is that the smaller the value $
u(y)$ is, the closer $y\in G$ is to the subgroup of $G$ defined by the equation $
u(x)= ot$, where $ ot$ is the bottom element of $L$. We test whether this notion is a suitable substitute for the usual notion of a subgroup (recovered by taking $L=\{ ot,	op\}$ with join as the sum), by showing that the form of proximity subgroups is noetherian. Intuitively, this means that proximity subgroups are as well suited for formulating and proving isomorphism theorems and homological diagram lemmas for groups as the usual subgroups are. We study several questions in relation to this, including what makes the noetherian form of usual subgroups special among all of these noetherian forms, and in fact, all noetherian forms of the category of groups.

papers.title: On rational representations and rational group algebra of $\operatorname{GL}_2(q)$
papers.abstract: In this article, we study rational representations of $G=\operatorname{GL}_2(q)$, where $q$ is a prime power. Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of $G$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. Then $\rho$ affords the character \[ \Omega(\chi)=m_{\mathbb{Q}}(\chi)\sum_{\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\chi)/\mathbb{Q})}\chi^{\sigma}, \] for some irreducible complex character $\chi$ of $G$, where $m_{\mathbb{Q}}(\chi)$ denotes the Schur index of $\chi$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, and conversely, every character of this form is afforded by an irreducible representation of $G$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. We obtain a combinatorial description for the counting of inequivalent irreducible $\mathbb{Q}$-representations of $G$ of each distinct degree. Furthermore, we briefly determine the rational character table of $G$ and present a method for constructing an irreducible rational matrix representation $\rho$ of $G$ affording the character $\Omega(\chi)$, where $\chi$ is an irreducible complex character of $G$ arising from parabolic induction. Finally, using the results on the rational representations of $G$, we derive an explicit combinatorial formula, depending only on $q$, for the Wedderburn decomposition of $\mathbb{Q}G$.

papers.title: On sinks and mirrors
papers.abstract:
Given a full rank sink recurrent cluster $\mathcal{A}$ variety, we prove that its wrapped Fukaya category is equivalent to the category of coherent sheaves on a stacky elaboration of the dual Fock-Goncharov cluster $\mathcal{X}$ variety.
  In particular, braid varieties for a semisimple group are mirror to the braid varieties for the Langlands dual group. Another example: for compact surfaces with no interior marked points, a least one marked point on each boundary component, and at least two marked points in total, the Fock-Goncharov moduli for SL(2) and PGL(2) are homologically mirror. The results were obtained in communion with ChatGPT Astra.

papers.title: On smooth affine surfaces with the cohomology of a smooth curve
papers.abstract: We prove that if a smooth affine complex surface has the same integral mixed Hodge structure as a smooth curve whose compactification is of positive genus, then it admits a smooth morphism to the curve with fibers isomorphic to $\mathbb{A}^1$. In particular, every such surface is the total space of a torsor for a line bundle on the curve. The motivation comes from Jouanolou's trick, to which this result gives a kind of converse in dimension $2$. We also give an example in the case of $\mathbb{P}^1$ which has the same integral mixed Hodge structure as $\mathbb{P}^1$ and simply connected but does not admit a smooth $\mathbb{A}^1$ fibration over $\mathbb{P}^1$.

papers.title: On some formality criteria for DG-Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We give some formality criteria for a differential graded Lie algebra to be formal. For instance, we show that a DG-Lie algebra L is formal if and only if the natural spectral sequence computing the Chevalley-Eilenberg cohomology H(L,L) degenerates at second page.

papers.title: On the Chow ring of very general abelian varieties and a question of Pirola
papers.abstract: We prove that for a very general abelian variety of dimension $\geq 4$, a divisor $D\in {\rm CH}^1(A)$ that satisfies $D^2=0$ in ${\rm CH}^2(A)$ is of torsion. The same result is also established for a very general Jacobian in genus $4$. We use then the second statement in order to prove a conjecture of Pirola, which states that any rational section of the Kummer fibration $K=J/\pm {\rm Id}\rightarrow \mathcal{M}_4$, where $J\rightarrow \mathcal{M}_4 $ is the Jacobian fibration, must be a multiple of the Griffiths-Pirola section given by the difference of the two trigonal divisors.

papers.title: On the Cohomological Amplitude of the Locally Analytic Jacquet--Langlands Functor
papers.abstract: We prove a local cohomological bound $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}(X,\mathcal F)\in D^{[0,\dim X]}$ for a pro-\'etale sheaf with a derived $p$-complete integral lattice whose modulo $p^m$ reductions are filtered colimits of finite local systems on an affinoid topologically of finite type over $C$. For $G=\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, with $n\geq2$ and $F/\mathbb Q_p$ finite, we apply these local bounds to variants of Scholze's Jacquet--Langlands functor $\mathrm{JL}_\mathscr{B}(\Pi):= R\Gamma_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}(\mathbb{P}^{n-1}_C,\mathcal{F}_{\Pi}\otimes^{L, \square}_{\mathbb{Q}_p}\mathscr{B})$ for $\mathscr{B}\in\{\mathbb{Q}_p, \widehat{\mathscr{O}}, \mathbb{B}_J\}$ and Banach or compact-type LB representations $\Pi$ of $G$, obtaining $\mathrm{JL}_{\mathscr{B}}(\Pi)\in D^{[0,2(n-1)]}$ for each choice of $\mathscr{B}$. We also prove that for arbitrary continuous principal series $I(\eta)=(\mathrm{Ind}_B^G\eta)^{\mathrm{cont}}$, we have $\mathrm{JL}(\mathrm{Ind}_B^G\eta)\in D^{[0, n]}$, while $\mathrm{JL}_{\widehat{\mathscr{O}}}(I(\eta)),\mathrm{JL}_{\mathbb{B}_J}(I(\eta))\in D^{[0, n-1]}$.

papers.title: On the Drinfeld formal group
papers.abstract: We identify Drinfeld's formal group on the prismatization of $\mathrm{Spf}\,\mathbb{Z}_p$ with a formal group arising from homotopy theory, given locally by the Quillen formal group of a decompleted variant of topological periodic cyclic homology. We also prove that this formal group extends to the syntomization of $\mathrm{Spf}\,\mathbb{Z}_p$, and that it admits a certain algebraization conjectured by Drinfeld.

papers.title: On the hit problem of rank five
papers.abstract: Let $P_q$ be the graded polynomial algebra $\mathbb F_2[x_1,x_2,\ldots ,x_q]$ over the prime field of two elements, $\mathbb F_2$, with the degree of each $x_i$ being 1. We study the {\it hit Peterson problem} of finding a minimal set of generators for $P_q$ as a module over the mod-$2$ Steenrod algebra, $\mathcal{A}.$ In this note, we present the minimal sets of $\mathcal{A}$-generators for $P_5$ in the cases where the degree are sufficiently general.

papers.title: On the Hodge, Tate, and standard conjectures for abelian varieties
papers.abstract: This is a report on two preprints of OpenAI, " Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties" and "The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties", placing them in context.

papers.title: On the quadratic length of plane Cremona maps of degree 4
papers.abstract:
Every non-linear plane Cremona map can be decomposed into quadratic maps, and the minimum number of quadratic maps required is called its quadratic length. It is known that plane Cremona maps of degree 3 have quadratic length either 2 or 3.
  In this paper, we study the quadratic length of plane Cremona maps $\varphi$ of degree 4. Recall that either $\varphi$ is de Jonqui\`eres, i.e. it has a base point of multiplicity 3, or it is not de Jonqui\`eres. In the latter case, $\varphi$ has quadratic length 2, whereas in the former case we prove that $\varphi$ has quadratic length 3, 4, or 5, and we classify those maps that reach the upper bound.

papers.title: On wall-crossing invariant combinations of Welschinger numbers for rational surfaces with a conic bundle
papers.abstract: We refine the real enumerative invariants insensitive to changes in the real structure introduced in our previous paper on del Pezzo surfaces, and extend these refined invariants to arbitrary rational surfaces. The construction involves a choice of an auxiliary conic bundle together with a Pin-structure. We prove that the resulting invariants are independent of these auxiliary choices and establish recursive relations for their computation.

papers.title: Orbit structures and complexity in Schubert and Richardson Varieties
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is twofold. Firstly, we provide a type-uniform formula for the torus complexity of the usual torus action on a Richardson variety, by developing the notion of algebraic dimensions of Bruhat intervals, strengthening a type $A$ result by Donten-Bury, Escobar and Portakal. In the process, we give an explicit description of the torus action on any Deodhar component as well as describe the root subgroups that comprise the component. Secondly, when a Levi subgroup in a reductive algebraic group acts on a Schubert variety, we exhibit a codimension preserving bijection between the Levi-Borel subgroup (a Borel subgroup in the Levi subgroup) orbits in the big open cell of that Schubert variety and torus orbits in the big open cell of a distinguished Schubert subvariety. This bijection has many applications including a type-uniform formula for the Levi-Borel complexity of the usual Levi-Borel subgroup action on a Schubert variety. We conclude by extending the Levi-Borel complexity results to a large class of Schubert varieties in the partial flag variety.

papers.title: Oversmoothing as Representation Degeneracy in Neural Sheaf Diffusion
papers.abstract: Neural Sheaf Diffusion (NSD) learns a task-adapted sheaf geometry for node classification. We connect the study of these learned geometries with Geometric Invariant Theory (GIT) to analyse their representation-theoretic structure and develop mechanisms for geometric control during training. Identifying cellular sheaves with representations of the incidence quiver connects direct-sum decompositions to the harmonic space and motivates the study of trivial or low-complexity summands as potential degeneration modes. We make this perspective concrete by focusing on the trivial representation: on an embedded copy, the sheaf Dirichlet energy reduces to weighted scalar graph energy. The GIT stability framework provides a criterion for excluding such copies within the semistable class. Using its moment-map characterisation of polystability, we construct differentiable surrogates that encourage the corresponding balance conditions. We identify an equal-stalk obstruction to assigning a destabilising weight to the trivial representation and show how nonuniform stalk dimensions remove it. Controlled energy-minimisation experiments reproduce trivial-component formation, while native feature-conditioned NSD experiments on heterophilic graphs show how moment-map regularisation changes the balance and Dirichlet-energy trajectories of learned geometries during training, alongside their classification behaviour.

papers.title: Path Types in Algebraic Type Theory
papers.abstract: A new approach to the semantics of identity types in intensional Martin-L\"of type theory is proposed, assuming only a category with finite limits and an interval. The specification of \emph{extensional} identity types in the original presentation of natural models paralleled that of the other type formers $\Sigma$ and $\Pi$, but the treatment of the \emph{intensional} case there was less uniform. It was later reformulated to an account based on polynomials; here a further improvement in the style of the other type formers is achieved by employing an interval, in order to give a single pullback specification of a model with \emph{path types}. The interval is also used to specify a (Hurewicz) fibration structure on the universe of the model. It is shown that the combination of these two conditions suffices to model the intensional identity rules, assuming only finite limits. The addition of an interval also relates the current treatment to that of cubical type theory.

papers.title: Period relations as period terms: linear independence at CM and Beta periods
papers.abstract: We prove linear independence results for periods of CM abelian varieties and Beta values by using a known relation between periods as the period term in the algebraic subgroup theorem. For example, $1$, $B(\frac27,\frac27)$, $B(\frac37,\frac37)$ and $B(\frac37,\frac37)/B(\frac17,\frac17)$ are linearly independent over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, and families of such relations attached to the CM types of $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_N)$ give the linear independence of $1$, a common ratio and $\kappa\ge2$ periods. The same method proves Waldschmidt's Conjecture 42 at six classes of CM ratios (for instance, $\wp(\log 2/\varpi)$ and $\wp(\log 3/\varpi)$ are not both algebraic on the lemniscatic curve) and several four exponentials statements at CM periods. All results are explicit consequences of theorems of Waldschmidt and of Roy and Waldschmidt.

papers.title: Poincar\'e duality and module topological complexity
papers.abstract: For every simply connected space $X$ of finite rational type with Poincar\'e duality cohomology, we prove $MTC(X)=TC_0(X)=TC_0^M(X)$: module, rational and monoidal rational topological complexity coincide. Neither formality nor finiteness of the total rational homotopy is required. For every rationally retractive map $f$ between simply connected spaces of finite rational type, we prove $relcat(f_Q)\le msecat(f_Q)+1$. This bound is sharp for rationally retractive maps. Both proofs reduce to the same question: can a module nullhomotopy taking values in a split Sullivan model be chosen with values in its kernel ideal? Comparing resolutions of consecutive ideal powers achieves this after increasing the exponent by one; for diagonals, Poincar\'e duality preserves the exponent. An ideal-preserving form of Hess's construction then converts the module nullhomotopy into a compatible algebra retraction.

papers.title: Presentations of inverse Artin monoids of type $D_n$ via cluster mutations
papers.abstract: Let $D_n^\varepsilon$ denote the Dynkin diagram of type $D_{n+1}$ with the endpoint $\varepsilon$ of its long branch frozen, and let $\mathcal{M}(D_n^\varepsilon)$ be the mutation class of any orientation of this diagram under mutations at mutable vertices. For each $\Gamma\in\mathcal{M}(D_n^\varepsilon)$, we define an inverse monoid $M_\Gamma$ by generators and relations determined by $\Gamma$. We prove that $M_\Gamma\cong M_{\mu_k(\Gamma)}$ for every mutable vertex $k$. Consequently, every quiver in this mutation class yields a presentation of the inverse Artin monoid of type $D_n$. Our argument establishes mutation invariance for the presentations of inverse Artin monoids of both types $A_n^\varepsilon$ and $D_n^\varepsilon$.

papers.title: Pretorsion theories and image-closed subcategories
papers.abstract: A pretorsion theory generalizes a torsion pair by allowing its two components to have a nonzero intersection, with morphisms factoring through the intersection playing the role of zero morphisms. In the module category of a finite-dimensional algebra, the first and second components of pretorsion theories are known to be the quotient-closed and submodule-closed subcategories, respectively. We show that the intersections of the two components are precisely the image-closed subcategories, namely those containing the image of every morphism between their objects, and that the pretorsion theories form a complete lattice. For a linearly oriented quiver of type A, we prove that the numbers of pretorsion theories and of image-closed subcategories are the Genocchi and median Genocchi numbers, respectively. Counting pretorsion theories by the number of indecomposable modules in their intersection, and image-closed subcategories by their number of indecomposable modules, yields the Gandhi polynomial refinements of Han and Zeng.

papers.title: Prime factors of fusion-category dimensions: weak group-theoreticity and decomposition
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be the Frobenius–Perron dimension of a weakly integral fusion category and $Q(D)$ its square-full part. For primes $p<q<r<s$ and nonnegative integers $a,b$, we prove that a braided category of dimension $D$ is weakly group-theoretical whenever $Q(D)\mid p^{5}q^{a}r^{b}$ or $Q(D)\mid p^{3}q^{3}r^{a}s^{b}$. Without a braiding assumption, $D\mid pqr^{a}s^{b}$ implies solvability. We also give criteria for adjoining a prime power of arbitrary exponent. For fixed $m$, the braided problem for dimensions dividing $\ell^{e}m$, with $\ell\nmid m$ prime and $e\ge 0$, reduces to finitely many dimensions. A braided category of dimension $D$ is weakly group-theoretical if $Q(D)<29160000$, and solvable if $Q(D)$ is odd and $Q(D)<6087156075$. Without a braiding assumption, the corresponding conclusions hold for $D<5400$ and for odd $D<121275$, respectively. We also obtain rank bounds and criteria for decomposing integral modular categories into braided factors.

papers.title: Propagation and Optimization of Low-Frequency Spectral Alignment in ReLU Networks on a Fixed Sample Graph
papers.abstract: We study how low-frequency structure, measured with respect to the Laplacian of a fixed graph built on the training samples, propagates through a ReLU network to the least-squares readout $g$, and how individual neurons $h=S\Phi\theta$ can be optimized to capture low-frequency eigenvectors. The readout error splits into a low-frequency part controlled by coverage (how well the feature span contains the low eigenvectors) and a high-frequency part controlled by the smoothness (Dirichlet energy) of the target. We prove an error bound that makes this precise, with coverage measured by the coverage gap, the largest principal-angle sine between the low eigenvectors and the feature span, and show that coverage can always be preserved across ReLU layers. Finally, we define a count $N_K$ of captured low-frequency features, relate it to our error bounds, and prove that error can be reduced to a smoothness component when $N_K$ captures every low frequency feature. Lastly, we show that a ReLU layer can strictly increase $N_K$ whenever the previous layer keeps the samples distinct and coverage is not yet full, that $2K+2$ neurons suffice to preserve coverage, that greedily chosen neurons drive the coverage gap down at rate $O(1/t)$ governed by a ReLU variation norm of the low eigenvectors, and that $t$ neurons can reduce the coverage gap no further than the $(t+1)$-st principal-angle sine.

papers.title: R(12,12) ≥ 1661 by extending the Mathon–Shearer coloring
papers.abstract: We prove that $R(12,12)\ge 1661$ by constructing a red/blue coloring of the edges of $K_{1660}$ with no monochromatic $K_{12}$. We start from a classical $(11,11)$-coloring on 1596 vertices, delete 21 of its vertices and add 85 new ones. Toward the remaining 1575 vertices, each new vertex has either the same colors as one of the deleted vertices or a single color. The deleted vertices include two pairs whose members have complementary colors toward every other vertex, and these pairs weaken the conditions that the new vertices must satisfy. The proof reduces to a finite check on the new vertices and is formally verified in Lean 4.

papers.title: Rational homotopy theory of flag manifolds
papers.abstract:
Let $G/P$ be a flag manifold with $G$ simple. We determine the rational homotopy groups $\pi _{\ast }(G/P)\otimes \mathbb{Q}$ and describe the rational cohomology ring $H^{\ast }(G/P;\mathbb{Q})$ solely in terms of the rational homotopy types of $G$ and $P$, respectively.
  The proof is based on the restrictions of basic Weyl invariants of $G$ to suitable simple factors of $P$, which also address a key nonvanishing issue not settled by earlier approaches of Meier, Shiga-Tezuka, Kotschick, and Terzic.

papers.title: Rational points on the non-split Cartan modular curve of level $121$
papers.abstract: We show that the modular curve $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^+(121)$, attached to the normalizer of a non-split Cartan subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Z}/121\mathbb{Z})$, has exactly $7$ rational points, all of them CM points. Together with the work of Rouse, Sutherland and Zureick-Brown, this completes the classification of the possible $11$-adic images of Galois of elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ without complex multiplication. We do not use a model of $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^+(121)$, which has genus $511$. Instead we use the map $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^+(121)\rightarrow X_{\mathrm{ns}}^+(11)$, whose target is an elliptic curve of rank $1$, a descent with the cusps of $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^+(11)$ and a Mordell-Weil sieve to reduce the problem to $7$ hyperelliptic curves of genus $5$ over a number field of degree $15$. We deal with these curves by a version of Stoll's Selmer group Chabauty method for the isogeny $1-\zeta_{11}$ of their Jacobians.

papers.title: Representation Varieties of Stacks and Trace Maps
papers.abstract: We define a derived stack $\mathscr{Rep}_n(X)$ which generalizes the assignment $A\leadsto \operatorname{Rep}_n(A)$ to an algebra of its derived $GL_n$-representation variety of arXiv:1112.1449 from algebras $A$ to perfect stacks $X$ over characteristic 0 fields. In the case of a quasi-projective classical scheme $X$, we show that $\mathscr{Rep}_n(X)$ admits a subfunctor $\operatorname{Quot}^{n,\text{fr}}_{\mathscr{O}_X^n}(X)\subset \mathscr{Rep}_n(X)$, which is in fact represented by a derived scheme almost of finite type. We further construct a Fourier-Mukai integral transform between the derived categories of quasi-coherent sheaves on $X$ and $\operatorname{Quot}^{n,\text{fr}}_{\mathscr{O}_X^n}(X)$ which induces a trace map at the level of Hochschild homology generalizing the trace morphism constructed in arXiv:1112.1449 (for finitely presented commutative algebras). We show that the subfunctor $\operatorname{Quot}^{n,\text{fr}}_{\mathscr{O}_X^n}(X)$ is a derived enhancement of the framed locus of the Quot scheme of points and that this derived scheme is a $GL_n$-torsor over the stack of coherent length $n$ torsion sheaves. Hence, this stack is an analog of the derived character stack for quasi-projective schemes, and we show that for smooth, Calabi-Yau $X$, it inherits a shifted symplectic structure in the sense of arXiv:1111.3209 from the one constructed in arXiv:1812.11913 on the moduli stack of perfect complexes with proper support. This structure is shown to give a generalization of the classical symplectic structure on character varieties of surfaces of genus 1 constructed by Goldman \cite{gold}.

papers.title: Representations of the Weyl algebra modulo $p^2$
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf{k}$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. Let $R=W_2(\mathbf{k})$ be the ring of Witt vectors of length $2$. In this note, we are concerned with the study of representations of the first Weyl algebra that are finite-rank free $R$-modules ($R$-lattices). Our main result shows that given an $R[x]$-lattice $V$, it admits a left module structure over the Weyl algebra (equivalently, an $R$-linear connection) if and only if all of its indecomposable summands have the form $R[x]\otimes_{R[x^p]}N$, where $N$ is an indecomposable $R[x^p]$-lattice of rank divisible by $p$. We also classify, up to isomorphism, all lattices over the $p$-Weyl algebra (defined by $[y,x]=p$) for which the action of $x$ modulo $p$ is regular nilpotent.

papers.title: Restrictions to a principal $A_1$-subgroup
papers.abstract:
We consider simple simply-connected algebraic groups $G$ over the complex numbers, and a principal $A_1$-subgroup $A \leq G$. We show that for most types of $G$ all its irreducible representations $V(\lambda)$ ($\lambda$ a dominant weight) are determined by their restrictions to $A$ up to graph automorphisms.
  The exceptions are groups $G$ of type $A_l$ with $l \geq 5$ and $G$ of type $D_l$ with $l = 4^m$ and $m \geq 2$.

papers.title: Rigidity does not imply substitution rigidity
papers.abstract: We obtain a negative answer to a question of Freudenburg concerning rigidity conditions for a polynomial. We construct a polynomial that does not lie in the kernel of any nonzero locally nilpotent derivation on the polynomial ring, but there exist an affine domain, algebraically independent elements and a locally nilpotent derivation such that the result of substituting elements into the polynomial lies in the kernel of that locally nilpotent derivation, but at least one of the substituted elements does not lie in that kernel.

papers.title: Second moments of pattern counts in dual Melas codewords
papers.abstract: Let $\alpha$ be a primitive element of $\mathbb{F}_{2^k}$ and, for $c\in\mathbb{F}_{2^k}^*$, let $S_c=(\mathrm{Tr}(\alpha^i+c\alpha^{-i}))_{0\le i\le 2^k-2}$ be the corresponding codeword of the dual Melas code. Let $X_{k,c}(w)$ be the number of occurrences of a uniformly random pattern $w\in\mathbb{F}_2^k$ in $S_c$. Sac Himelfarb and Schwartz conjectured that $X_{k,c_k}$ converges to the Poisson law $\mathcal P(1)$ for every choice of $c_k\in\mathbb{F}_{2^k}^*$; they proved that the second factorial moment satisfies $\limsup M_2\le 2$, and $M_2\to1$ for almost every sequence $(c_k)$. We prove that $|M_2^{(k,c)}-1|\le 2^{-(1/22+o(1))k}$ uniformly in $c\in\mathbb{F}_{2^k}^*$ and in the primitive element $\alpha$. Thus the second factorial moment converges to $1$ for every sequence $(c_k)$. The proof expresses $M_2$ through a norm form of the quadratic extension $\mathbb{F}_2(x)/\mathbb{F}_2(x+x^{-1})$, which turns it into a bilinear Kloosterman sum of full length, and bounds the latter in characteristic two. We also show that the counts $N_w(S_c)$, as functions of $(w,c)$, are the fibre sizes of a family of quadratic maps, and deduce that for almost every sequence of patterns $w_k$ the first two factorial moments of $c\mapsto N_{w_k}(S_c)$ converge to $1$, as they would under the Poisson law conjectured by Sac Himelfarb and Schwartz for fixed patterns.

papers.title: Secondary Stiefel-Whitney numbers and corresponding cobordism groups
papers.abstract: For every relation $R$ between Stiefel-Whitney numbers of closed $(n+1)$-manifolds we consider an associated invariant $\varkappa_R$ of null-cobordant $n$-manifolds with a certain additional structure. For $n=2k-1$ and $R = w_{n+1}+v_k^2$ the invariant $\varkappa_R$ equals the Kervaire semi-characteristic. In addition, we construct the cobordism group $\Omega_n^R$, which extends the unoriented cobordism group $\Omega_n^O$. We show that $\varkappa_R$ is a complete invariant of $R$-cobordism classes of null-cobordant $n$-manifolds. We prove that our invariant $\varkappa_R$ and $R$-cobordism class of manifold are quadratic in the sense of Gusarov-Vassiliev-Podkorytov.

papers.title: Sections of the Kottwitz homomorphism and affine pinnings
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group split over $\mathbb{Z}$. The Kottwitz homomorphism identifies the group of connected components of the loop group of $G$ with the group $\Omega$ of length zero elements of the extended affine Weyl group. We show that this homomorphism always has a homomorphic section, and that the section can be chosen inside the normalizer of $T$ in $G(\mathbb{Z}[t,t^{-1}])$. We then ask whether the section can be chosen to preserve an affine pinning. This is possible if no simple factor of $G$ is of type $B_{2m}$ or $C_{2m}$. It is impossible for $(SL_2\times Sp_{2n})/\mu_2$ and $(SL_2\times Spin_{2n+1})/\mu_2$ when $n$ is even. We show that the obstructions for $G$ and for its Langlands dual group are dual to each other, and we compute them by a lattice computation with a Coxeter element. As an application, we show that the component group of the centralizer of any semisimple element lifts to the centralizer. Under the same condition on the simple factors, the lift can be chosen to preserve a pinning of the neutral component.

papers.title: Semiampleness of Hodge line bundles and b-semiampleness of the moduli part
papers.abstract:
We give proofs of Hodge semiampleness and b-semiampleness without using o-minimality. We establish a geometric semiampleness criterion for line bundles on proper algebraic spaces. Let $(X,D)$ be a log smooth pair with $X$ a proper algebraic space. For an integral polarizable pure variation of Calabi--Yau type on $X\setminus D$ with unipotent local monodromy, let $L$ be its extended highest Hodge line. If $L$ is numerically integrable and has torsion combinatorial monodromy, then $L$ is semiample. We also prove semiampleness of extended Griffiths lines. We construct normal projective period compactifications on which a positive power of the Griffiths line extends to an ample line bundle.
  As an application, we prove that the moduli b-divisor $\mathbf{M}$ of a projective lc-trivial fibration over a normal algebraic variety is b-semiample, provided that the generic boundary is effective. Suppose further that the geometric generic pair is klt and its boundary is big, with nonzero coefficients in a fixed finite set $I\subset(0,1)\cap\mathbb{Q}$. Then $c\mathbf{M}$ is b-Cartier and b-free for an integer $c>0$ depending only on the relative dimension and $I$. We extend b-semiampleness to analogous projective fibrations over normal complex analytic bases, assuming a global relative polarization and an invertible log pluricanonical sheaf pulled back from the base.

papers.title: Semihomogenous vector bundles, $\mathbb Q$-twisted sheaves, duality, and linear systems on abelian varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper, we point out the natural relation between $\mathbb Q$-twisted objects of the derived category of abelian varieties, cohomological rank functions, and semihomogeneous vector bundles. We apply this to two basic classes of objects, corresponding to each other via the Fourier-Mukai-Poincar\'e transform: positive twists of the ideal sheaf of one point and of the evaluation complexes of ample simple semihomogeneous vector bundles. This naturally leads to the introduction of $\mathbb Q^{\ge 0}$- graded section modules associated to line bundles on abelian varieties built by means of semihomogeneous vector bundles (containing the usual section rings). We prove a duality relation between such modules associated to dual polarizations, which is not visible at the level of the usual section rings. Other applications include formulas relating the thresholds of relevant cohomological rank functions appearing in this context. As a consequence we show a lower bound for the base point free threshold of a polarization in function of its type, and some obstructions to surjectivity of multiplication maps of global sections of certain line bundles.

papers.title: Semisimple Deformations of Contraction Algebras for Smooth Threefold Flops
papers.abstract: Building on Bryan--Katz--Leung, Hua--Toda and Kawamata, we study deformations of contraction algebras and the local geometry of the scheme of associative algebra laws. Let $A$ be the basic contraction algebra of a completed projective flopping contraction of a smooth complex threefold. We construct a finite free polynomial family that is constant and semisimple away from the origin, with the original curve projectors fixed. For each restricted positive root $\beta=(\beta_i)$, with coordinates indexed by the retained vertices, the split generic fibre has $n_\beta$ matrix blocks of size $\sum_i\beta_i$, and the labelled projector $e_i$ has rank $\beta_i$ on each block. Here $n_\beta$ is the corresponding genus-zero Gopakumar--Vafa invariant. If the geometric generic fibre of a finite free associative formal deformation of $A$ is semisimple, it has the same matrix factors, and any lifts of the original projectors have the same ranks on those factors. The scheme of associative algebra laws is smooth at $A$. The closure of the corresponding semisimple orbit is its unique irreducible component through $A$. The proof uses the curve divisors of Katz--Morrison and Nabijou--Wemyss, presentations of the universal contraction quotient and its cocenter, and the orbit method of Jelisiejew--Smoktunowicz. These presentations prove the geometric Hua--Toda flatness assertions. In the geometric families considered here, the relative contraction algebra, its centre and its cocenter are finite free over arbitrary complete Noetherian local complex bases. On a smooth open neighbourhood of $A$ in the scheme of algebra laws, the centres and cocenters form dual vector bundles compatible with arbitrary base change. For the type $D$ algebras $D_{n,2}$ with $n\ge2$, the centre morphism gives counterexamples to the smoothness assertion in Conjecture 1.4(2) of Jelisiejew--Smoktunowicz.

papers.title: Seven Research Directions in Differential Geometry and Differential Topology Enabled by AI
papers.abstract: This article presents seven AI-generated research directions in differential geometry and differential topology, each centered on a proposed research object or formulation. For each direction, we provide basic definitions and theorems, discuss connections with existing mathematical problems and theories, and outline questions for further study. The definitions introduced in these seven directions are relatively new. The article is intended as a collection of AI-generated research guides rather than a conventional research paper.

papers.title: Shared triangular sides in pseudoline arrangements
papers.abstract: Let $d$ be the number of edges incident to two bounded triangular faces in a finite affine arrangement of pseudolines, with each pair crossing exactly once and with only double and triple crossings. If $t_3$ is the number of triple crossings, we prove $d\leq 3t_3$, answering the compensation question of Parpalak and Utkin. The proof distributes charge along the normalized boundary of the union of triangular faces. A double crossing incident to four triangles is treated by restricting the arrangement to the four pseudolines supporting their opposite sides. This restriction provides two boundary edges whose unused endpoint charges pay for the crossing.

papers.title: Sharp minima of higher Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated singularities
papers.abstract: We determine the minimum higher Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated complex polynomial singularities with fixed ambient dimension and multiplicity. A Fermat polynomial of multiplicity $m$, perturbed by the $(m+1)$-st power of a linear form, attains both minimum sequences at every order. These values remain the minima at each prescribed total degree $d>m$; the homogeneous case $d=m$ has a separate Tjurina formula. The proof expresses the Tjurina defect through multiplication in the filtered Milnor algebra and uses the monomial strong Lefschetz theorem to attain the resulting rank bound. We also determine the associated graded higher Tjurina algebras of this family and show that they are unchanged by terms of order at least $m+2$.

papers.title: Sharp thresholds for five-colour cube assemblies
papers.abstract: We determine the least pool sizes guaranteeing a frame or a complete $a\times b\times c$ box from unit cubes whose faces use all five colours of a fixed palette, for every $a,b,c\ge2$. Proper rotations are allowed; the target has monochromatic exterior faces using all five colours. The frame threshold is $\max\{15,4(a+b+c)-16,2(a+b+c)+1\}$, and the complete-box threshold is $\max\{abc,15,2(a+b+c)+1\}$. The proof combines a certified fifteen-cube corner theorem with elementary Hall arguments and a uniform three-variety obstruction. It completes the five-colour frame column left open by Berkove, Eickemeyer and Schulman (2018). All threshold statements are formalised in Lean. A fixed-size flow formulation decides feasibility and constructs assemblies in time linear in the explicit source list. We also determine the corner thresholds when the number of source varieties is bounded, and classify all fourteen-cube obstructions into 56 classes under common colour relabelling and simultaneous reflection, described by three structural forms. The minimum size of a collection capable of reproducing every $2\times2\times2$ target is also fifteen.

papers.title: Simple algebraic groups with good reduction, the genus problem, and unramified cohomology
papers.abstract: We obtain a number of new results on the arithmetic of linear algebraic groups over higher-dimensional fields. In particular, we resolve some key open questions over 2-dimensional global fields, such as the finiteness of the genus of spinor groups of quadratic forms of dimension $\geq 10$. We also extend various finiteness results to new classes of fields, including function fields of $p$-adic surfaces. Our arguments rely in a crucial way on new finiteness results for unramified cohomology.

papers.title: Singularities in leaf closures on complex surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove a geometric and dynamical criterion excluding minimal sets contained in the regular locus of a holomorphic foliation on a compact complex surface. In particular, we prove that every Jouanolou foliation of degree at least two has no exceptional minimal set. We also give an explicit lower bound, growing linearly with the degree, for the number of singularities in every regular leaf closure of a Jouanolou foliation. This bound persists under small perturbations, as does the existence of a nonempty open saturated set whose leaves accumulate at all singularities. Under finite pullback unramified over the singular set, the bound is multiplied by the degree of the normalised component over the base leaf. Together with a general persistence theorem, this yields nonempty analytic open sets of foliations on every smooth projective surface with arbitrarily large uniform lower bounds on the number of singularities in their regular leaf closures. On double-plane K3 surfaces, we obtain foliations with ample canonical bundle and explicitly describe and count their singularities.

papers.title: Smale's mean value constant (1981) exceeds 1.1559
papers.abstract: We prove that Smale's mean value constant exceeds $1.1559837$, improving the bound $1.1018$ of Jatar and Ng. Smale proved in 1981 that for every complex polynomial $P$ of degree at least $2$ and every point $z$ with $P'(z)\neq0$, some critical point $\zeta$ of $P$ satisfies $|P(z)-P(\zeta)|\le K\,|z-\zeta|\,|P'(z)|$ with $K=4$, and he conjectured that $K=1$ suffices. The best constant $K^*$ is called Smale's mean value constant. Smale's conjecture is false: a proof that $K^*>1$ appeared in 2026. Jatar and Ng showed that every pair $(W,B)$ of a normalized univalent map $W$ of the unit disk and a finite Blaschke product $B$ with $B(0)>0$, such that $(WB)'$ has no zero in the disk, gives $K^*\ge1/B(0)$. We construct such a pair explicitly, with $B$ of degree two, from a polynomial of degree $18$ with Gaussian rational coefficients, and we verify the required properties by a computation in exact arithmetic. Since the best constant $K(d)$ for degree $d$ is nondecreasing in $d$ (Crane), $K(d)$ also exceeds $1.1559837$ for all large $d$. All theorems, lemmas and corollaries of this paper, and the results of Jatar and Ng that it uses, are also proved in the Lean 4 proof assistant and checked with the Lean comparator.

papers.title: Some examples of DG-Lie formality transfer
papers.abstract: We give a convenient reformulation, a slight generalization and some applications of the formality transfer theorem for DG-Lie algebras.

papers.title: Spectral synthesis for the Báez–Duarte step space
