papers.abstract: We prove that the closed Báez–Duarte subspace of the Mellin step space is exactly the common kernel of the derivative evaluations prescribed by the zeros of the Riemann zeta function in $\operatorname{Re}s>1/2$, with their multiplicities. No finiteness or sparsity assumption on this zero set is required. The proof combines a uniform fractional regularity estimate for Mellin transforms of step functions with a comparison obtained by reflecting zeros in a shifted vertical line. These estimates produce a holomorphic Hardy-space family whose membership in the Báez–Duarte subspace continues from large positive shifts to every sufficiently small positive shift. A uniformly bounded weak limit then gives the synthesis theorem.

papers.title: Spectrally Simple Spectra without Irreducible Nonnegative Realizations
papers.abstract: We give a counterexample to a conjecture of Johnson, Marijuán, and Pisonero: we show that the spectrum $\{1,1/2,\pm i/\sqrt3\}$ is realizable and spectrally simple, but has no irreducible nonnegative realization. More generally, we prove their nonexistence conjecture for an order-four boundary family.

papers.title: Stretched near-groups
papers.abstract: We study stretched near-group fusion categories over $\mathbb{C}$ of type $G+k|G|$ for abelian groups $G$ and positive integers $k$, describing the structure of the double including fusion rules, modular data, and Frobenius--Schur indicators under a variety of assumptions. For cyclic $G$, when enough invertible objects exist in the double, we describe all associated de-equivariantizations which connect the existence of stretched near-group fusion categories to the existence of other stretched quadratic categories. All of our results apply to the case $k=1$. In particular, the known existence of $C_{m^2}+m^2$ near-group categories for all positive integers $m$ implies the existence of Haagerup--Izumi fusion categories for all cyclic groups. As a further application, we provide a general conductor bound severely restricting the existence of stretched near-group categories, and for infinitely many abelian groups $G$ of square order, among them $C_4\times C_2^{2j}$ with $j\geq2$, we show that a near-group fusion category $G+k|G|$ exists if and only if $k=0$.

papers.title: Structural Reductions for Lusztig’s Conjectures in Types (B_n), (\widetilde B_n), and (\widetilde C_n)
papers.abstract: We develop structural reductions for Lusztig’s conjectures P1–P15 for unequal-parameter Hecke algebras of finite type (B_n) and nonextended affine types (\widetilde B_n) and (\widetilde C_n). The results include integral parabolic propagation mechanisms, reductions of P15 to constant leading-coefficient identities, spectral degree bounds, and finite-facet attainment criteria connecting affine tempered representations with the original Kazhdan–Lusztig filtration. Exact computations verify the relevant identities in the recorded finite-rank cases. These results produce internally audited proof candidates and isolate the remaining comparison and attainment problems required for unconditional all-rank statements.

papers.title: Superlinear regularity of Frobenius powers on a normal hypersurface
papers.abstract: We give answers to four questions on linear bounds for Frobenius powers. Let $\mathfrak m$ denote the homogeneous maximal ideal. We construct a height-two prime $I$ in a geometrically normal four-dimensional graded hypersurface $R$ of characteristic two such that, for every power $q\geq16$ of four, the Loewy length of $H^0_{\mathfrak m}(R/I^{[q]})$ is at least $q^{3/2}/8-1$. Thus no fixed integer $C$ gives annihilation by $\mathfrak m^{Cq}$ for all $q$, as required by the Hochster--Huneke condition $(\mathrm{LC})$. The same construction gives superlinear lower bounds for the Castelnuovo--Mumford regularity in Katzman's question, for the exponents of the embedded primary components in the question of Smith and Swanson, and for the degree in the least variable in Katzman's Gr\"obner basis conjecture. The bounds follow from the degree of the kernel line bundle of a multiplication pencil associated to a family of plane quartics.

papers.title: The 57 Grothendieckian Problems: Open Problems for Mathematics and Machine Reasoning from the Grothendieckian Programme
papers.abstract: We state fifty-seven open problems drawn from the seven works of the Grothendieckian Programme (34 volumes, 26,021 pages, released openly in October 2026 as first drafts that have not been peer-reviewed). Thirty-five come from the two works on the architecture of a reasoning system and twenty-two from the five works that each take a named conjecture or programme as research subject; no problem is one of those conjectures. Each problem is stated in the words of its source, located by work, chapter and page, given the status the source assigns it, and paired with a criterion that decides when it is solved, a note on existing work and the date of a literature check. The problems are of three kinds: twenty-five mathematical problems, nineteen machine problems with success criteria fixed in advance, and thirteen formalization problems for Lean 4 and Mathlib. Every quotation from the sources has been checked against the published PDFs, and each problem has been checked against the literature as of 28 October 2026; a machine-readable version accompanies the paper.

papers.title: The arithmetic de Rham stack
papers.abstract: We define and study the arithmetic de Rham stack $X^{\operatorname{arith}}$ of a scheme $X$ over a field of characteristic $p$, and analyze its relation with related stacks such as the Hyodo--Kato stack. We show that $X^{\operatorname{arith}}$ gives a stack-theoretic approach to rigid cohomology and its coefficients, known as overconvergent isocrystals and arithmetic $D$-modules, which avoids the long-standing problem of frame-choosing in earlier approaches. We finally give some arithmetic applications of our formalism, such as a proof of Berthelot's conjecture on the preservation of overconvergent isocrystals by smooth proper pushforward.

papers.title: The Bruce-Roberts number of holomorphic 1-forms along complex analytic varieties
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of the \textit{Bruce--Roberts number} for holomorphic 1-forms relative to complex analytic varieties. Our main result shows that the Bruce--Roberts number of a 1-form $\omega$ relative to a complex analytic hypersurface $X$ with an isolated singularity can be expressed in terms of the \textit{Gom\'ez-Mont--Seade--Verjovsky index} of $\omega$ along $X$, the \textit{Milnor number} of $\omega$ and the \textit{Tjurina number} of $X$. This result allows us to recover known formulas for the Bruce--Roberts number of a holomorphic function along $X$ and to establish connections between this number, the radial index, and the local Euler obstruction of $\omega$ along $X$. Moreover, we present applications to both global and local holomorphic foliations in complex dimension two.

papers.title: The Cereceda (2007) conjecture holds for bipartite 2-degenerate graphs
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$ and a positive integer $k$, the $k$-recolouring graph $\mathcal{R}_{k}(G)$ has the proper $k$-colourings of $G$ as vertices, two of them adjacent when they differ at exactly one vertex. A graph is $d$-degenerate if each of its non-empty subgraphs has a vertex of degree at most $d$. The Cereceda (2007) conjecture states that, for fixed $d$ and $k \ge d+2$, the diameter of $\mathcal{R}_{k}(G)$ is $O(n^2)$ for every $d$-degenerate graph $G$ on $n$ vertices. For $d = 2$, the conjecture was known to hold for $k \ge 5$ by a result of Cereceda; for $k = 4$, the best bound known for all $2$-degenerate graphs is $O(n^3)$, due to Bousquet and Heinrich. We prove that the diameter of $\mathcal{R}_{4}(G)$ is at most $2n(n+1)$ for every bipartite $2$-degenerate graph $G$ on $n$ vertices; hence the conjecture holds for these graphs. We also show that the order $n^2$ cannot be improved for this class, even for graphs of girth $6$. For the upper bound, we fix an ordering of the vertices in which each vertex has at most two later neighbours. In $n$ stages, we transform any proper $4$-colouring into the colouring in which every vertex has the least colour not used by its later neighbours, recolouring each vertex at most twice per stage. Both of our bounds have also been proved in the Lean proof assistant.

papers.title: The cohomology of finite simple groups is unbounded
papers.abstract: In every fixed positive degree, we show that the cohomology of finite simple groups, algebraic groups and quantum groups, with coefficients in simple modules, can have arbitrarily large dimension. In particular, we disprove Guralnick's conjecture.

papers.title: The finite projective classification of complex spinors via momentum maps
papers.abstract: We describe the projective orbits of complex spinors from the point of view of the momentum map. We treat the irreducible spin modules in odd dimensions 1,3,5,7,9,11 and the half-spin modules in even dimensions 2,4,6,8,10,12,14, which are the only cases with finitely many orbits. In the Clifford--Fock model, we construct representatives as sums of pure basis spinors, and the coefficients are chosen so that the representative is a critical point of the squared norm of the momentum map. The resulting momentum values in a fixed Weyl chamber distinguish the orbits. Completeness follows from Vinberg's theory of graded Lie algebras and stabilizer actions, independently of the classical spinor classifications. We recover the classical counts of 1,1,1,2,3,5 orbits in the odd cases and 1,1,1,2,2,4,9 in the even cases, and compute the projective dimension of every orbit. In dimension fourteen we also determine the closure order of the orbits, using the fact that the minimum of the squared momentum norm increases strictly under degeneration.

papers.title: The Fourier kernel and invariant trace formula of $\rm{GL}(3)$
papers.abstract: Trace formula is an important method to study the Langlands program. Arthur obtains the existence of stable trace formula for connected reductive group. In this paper, we will give the explicit invariant trace formula of GL(3). For general reductive groups, Arthur gave an inductive proof of the existence of the invariant trace formula and provided explicit examples for GL(2). For GL(3), we successively compute the invariant distributions, give all the Fourier kernels for the GL(2) cases, and finally obtain the concrete invariant trace formula.

papers.title: The Grothendieckian Programme: An Overview — Seven Open Works on Mathematics and Machine Reasoning
papers.abstract: The Grothendieckian Programme is a series of seven works on machine reasoning about mathematics (34 volumes, 26,021 pages), released openly on Zenodo in October 2026 with an overview volume. Two of the works specify a reasoning architecture — a core that holds mathematical worlds as typed, versioned and verifiable objects, and a kernel that reasons inside such worlds by sites, sheaves and descent. Five apply one method, recursive mathematical discovery, to the Riemann Hypothesis, the conjecture of Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer, the Hodge conjecture, the abc conjecture and the Langlands programme, and record what it proves, what it reduces to stated hypotheses and what it leaves open. This paper describes the architecture, the five research subjects, the method, the published corpus and the open process by which the works are to be reviewed and continued. None of the works claims a proof of any of these conjectures; they are first drafts and have not been peer-reviewed.

papers.title: The Logical Anatomy of Optimization: Reverse Mathematics, Proof Mining, and the Price of Convergence
papers.abstract: Optimization theory proves three kinds of theorems: that optimal points exist, that algorithms converge to them, and that optimality can be certified by duality. We measure how much mathematics each kind needs, using reverse mathematics, Weihrauch complexity and proof mining, and assemble the answers, old and new, into one map stated in the language of optimization. Compactness makes existence cost weak Kőnig's lemma, but convexity (and, format by format, tameness) makes it cheap: we show that $\mathsf{RCA}_0$ proves that convex functions on $[0,1]$ attain their minima (and on $[0,1]^n$, for each fixed $n$, given a modulus of uniform continuity), and that $\mathsf{RCA}_0$ proves linear programming duality and the minimax theorem for real data of every size. Convergence costs more: it follows from results of Kohlenbach and Neumann that convergence of gradient descent for convex smooth functions on $\mathbb{R}$ is equivalent to $\mathsf{ACA}_0$. We explain this by a selection principle: what costs is the particular minimizer the algorithm selects, and uniqueness or an error bound removes the cost. Below convergence lies finitary information. Gradient descent in $\mathbb{R}^d$ has at most $2C_dD/\varepsilon$ fluctuations of size $\varepsilon$, with $C_d$ depending only on $d$, which yields rates of metastability; no such bound is dimension-free, by the span-restriction argument behind performance estimation; and the limits of gradient descent on computable instances have d.c.e. coordinates, a proper subclass of the limit-computable reals. The map also covers Ekeland's variational principle (up to $\Pi^1_1\text{-}\mathsf{CA}_0$), separation theorems, Kőnig duality ($\mathsf{ATR}_0$), proof-mined rates for fixed-point iterations, and the feasible world, where local search captures the $\mathsf{NP}$ search problems provably total in $T^1_2$ and approximate stationary points of smooth functions are complete for $\mathsf{CLS}=\mathsf{PPAD}\cap\mathsf{PLS}$. We close with five principles and open problems.

papers.title: The L’vov–Kaplansky Conjecture for Matrices of Sufficiently Large Order
papers.abstract: For each positive degree, the L’vov–Kaplansky conjecture holds over arbitrary fields in all matrix sizes beyond a threshold depending only on the degree. In these sizes the image of a nonzero multilinear polynomial is the traceless subspace if every cyclic coefficient sum vanishes, and the full matrix algebra otherwise.

papers.title: The Mesirov-Sweet property over F_2 up to degree 33, with two quotients of degree two up to degree 28
papers.abstract: For a monic polynomial g in F_2[T] of degree d, the conjecture of Mesirov and Sweet asserts that there is f in F_2[T], coprime to g with deg f < d, such that every partial quotient of the continued fraction of f/g has degree at most 2. We check by exhaustive computation that this holds for every g of degree at most 33. We also check that for every g of degree at most 28 one can choose f so that all partial quotients are linear except at most two, which have degree 2. The computations combine exhaustive enumeration of fixed degree patterns, explicit certificates for the polynomials not reached by the patterns, and two separately written enumeration programs whose outputs coincide bit for bit. All programs are provided.

papers.title: The Minimum Canonical Volume of Threefolds of General Type
papers.abstract: We prove the sharp lower bound $vol(X) \geq 1/420$ for every smooth complex projective threefold $X$ of general type.

papers.title: The moduli stack of affine bundles with fixed linearisation type
papers.abstract:
The goal of this article is the classification of affine bundles with fixed linearisation type over a compact complex manifold $X$. More precisely, let $E$ be a fixed holomorphic vector bundle over $X$ and $\mathcal{E}$ the associated locally free sheaf. We will assume that there exists an effective divisor $D$ on $X$ such that $H^1(X,\mathcal{E}(D))=0$. This condition is always satisfied when $X$ is a projective complex manifold.
  We define in a natural way the moduli stack of affine bundles on $X$ whose linearisation is isomorphic to $E$, and we prove that this moduli stack is isomorphic to the quotient stack $\big[H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D)_D)/H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D))\ltimes \mathrm{Aut}(E)\big]$ of the complex vector space $H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D)_D)$ by the semi-direct product of the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(E)$ (which is always an affine algebraic group) by the complex vector space $H^0(X,{\cal E}(D))$. Our isomorphism is obtained by constructing explicitly comparison functors $\mathscr{A}$, $\mathscr{T}$ between the two stacks and explicit natural isomorphisms $\mathscr{A}\circ\mathscr{T}\stackrel{\simeq}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{id}$, $\mathrm{id} \stackrel{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}\mathscr{T}\circ\mathscr{A}$.

papers.title: The necklace of a rational right triangle: exact counting and complete periodicity
papers.abstract: Let $T$ be a right triangle with acute angle $\alpha$, $2\alpha/\pi = P/Q$ in lowest terms. The Katok--Zemlyakov unfolding of $T$, quotiented by its holonomy involution, is a necklace of $Q$ kites: an explicit genus-zero half-translation surface in the stratum $Q(P-2, Q-P-2, -1^Q)$, whose kites glue in steps of $P$ and whose interfaces have explicit transverse measures. We use it to count the cells into which the vertices of $T$ cut the beam perpendicular to each side. For a completely periodic direction class the separatrix diagram has exactly $Q$ edges, and sorting them by the involution gives the identity $Q = h + f + 2p$ ($h$ sides of $T$ in the class, $f$ extra cells of the perpendicular beams, $p$ involution-swapped edge pairs). When $p = 0$ it is a covering law: the perpendicular beams of a class cut $Q - 1$ or $Q + 1$ cells in total at odd $Q$, according to the class, and $Q$ at even $Q$; with no hypothesis the shortfall is even, non-negative, and zero only on a completely periodic class. Complete periodicity of a class — that almost every trajectory in it meets a side at a right angle — is equivalent to $p = 0$ and to the covering law (on two-beam classes off the Veech locus, one direction assumes an orphan branch, which companion papers prove at broad classes of centres); it fails at $8/15$. For the beam perpendicular to a leg the count $n(P/Q)$ is at most $Q - 1$ at every centre and is known exactly on the Veech locus $\min(P, Q-P) \leq 2$; off it we prove $n(3/Q) \leq 2\cdot\text{round}(Q/3) - 1$ for $Q \geq 5$, with equality exactly under complete periodicity, and $n(5/(5m+1)) = 5$ for every $m \geq 3$. Finally, every periodic billiard path of a rational right triangle in a mirror direction meets a side at a right angle.

papers.title: The rank of the Fano normal function via the Fermat cubic
papers.abstract: We prove that the canonical derivative of the Fano normal function has rank ten at the Fermat cubic threefold. This yields a direct proof of its generic maximal rank, a result also implied by a general theorem of Gao--Zhang. Our approach combines Hain's equivariance principle with an explicit representation-theoretic computation and the nonvanishing of the Griffiths infinitesimal invariant established by Collino--Naranjo--Pirola.

papers.title: The rational points of the non-split Cartan modular curve of level 121
papers.abstract: We prove that the modular curve $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^{+}(121)$ of the normalizer of a non-split Cartan subgroup of level 121, of genus 511, has exactly seven rational points, all of them CM. This is the level 121 case of a conjecture of Rouse, Sutherland and Zureick-Brown, and with their theorem it determines the 11-adic images of Galois of non-CM elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$. The Jacobian has rank equal to the genus. We work at the primes 17 and 43, at each of which one Hecke block of the Mordell–Weil group has logarithm divisible by $p^2$ while its $p$-adic height has valuation exactly one. A comparison of valuations in the quadratic Chabauty identity then shows that the residue disc of each CM point holds no other rational point, with no computation of the local height at $p$, no basis of the Mordell–Weil group and no model of the curve. The inputs come from expansions of differentials at CM points and from a formula we prove for intersection numbers of CM divisors under Hecke correspondences on $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^{+}(\ell^e)$, at every prime $v \ne \ell$, and at $v = \ell$ when $\ell \ge 7$, $\ell \equiv 3 \bmod 4$ and $e \le 2$.

papers.title: The ribbon category of representations of a crossed module
papers.abstract: The theory of representations of a crossed module is a direct generalization of the theory of representations of groups. For a finite group G, the Drinfeld quantum double of the group G is a Hopf algebra that represents a special case of crossed module of finite groups. Here we study how to extend the construction of the Drinfeld quantum double for any other kind of crossed module of finite groups. This leads to a Hopf algebra D(G,H) that presents similarities with a Drinfeld double. We then study simple subalgebras of D(G,H) and give two isomorphisms for the decomposition into a product of simple subalgebras. We then study the category D(G,H)-mod^Fd of finite dimensional modules over D(G,H), which turns out to be isomorphic to the category of finite dimensional representations of finite crossed modules of groups. These categories being monoidal, we also study links between direct sums of simple objects and tensor products of simple objects and give some results for a Clebsch-Gordan formula. We, in this context, present and develop the character theory for representations of crossed modules of finite groups, and detail the proofs. We then study the category itself, which leads to some ribbon invariants.

papers.title: The Rising-Sea Theses: Twelve Theses on Mathematics and Machine Reasoning
papers.abstract: The Grothendieckian Programme is a set of seven works on machine reasoning about mathematics (34 volumes, 26,021 pages), released openly in October 2026 as first drafts that have not been peer-reviewed. This paper draws from them twelve theses on how mathematics and machine reasoning should be combined. Each thesis is stated in one sentence, argued, tied to the passages of the seven works on which it rests, related to existing work, and paired with an observation that would refute it. The theses concern the unit of mathematical knowledge for a reasoning system, the place of epistemic status, the latent space of mathematical reasoning, attention, failure, authority, and the method of discovery. The paper adds no mathematical result to the seven works; none of them claims a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, the Hodge conjecture, the abc conjecture or the Langlands correspondence.

papers.title: Topological symmetric and braid homologies
papers.abstract: We identify topological symmetric homology as the free $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-algebra on an $\mathbb{E}_1$-algebra and topological braid homology as the free $\mathbb{E}_2$-algebra on an $\mathbb{E}_1$-algebra. In this way, topological symmetric homology and topological braid homology can be regarded as variants of $1$-dimensional representation homology. In order to identify topological braid homology as the free $\mathbb{E}_2$-algebra on an $\mathbb{E}_1$-algebra, we prove that the $\mathbb{E}_2$-monoidal envelope of the associative operad can be identified with the braided crossed simplicial group. Using this, we also compute the topological braid homology of grouplike $\mathbb{E}_1$-spaces. Further, we develop computational tools for topological symmetric and braid homologies. These tools allow us to perform low-degree computations of topological symmetric homology and prove that it is not Morita invariant. We also compute the topological $\Delta \mathbf{G}$-homology of Thom spectra in general and produce explicit formulas in the case of topological symmetric and braid homologies.

papers.title: Torsion of elliptic curves over number fields of degree $10$
papers.abstract: We determine all the groups that appear as the torsion group of an elliptic curve over a number field of degree $10$. There are $69$ such groups. For $4$ of them, namely $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/26\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/15\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/18\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/12\mathbb{Z}$, we also determine all the elliptic curves over number fields of degree $10$ that realize them, and there are only finitely many. These four groups were not known to occur over number fields of degree $10$. The proofs combine the global method of Derickx, Hecke sieves, formal immersion criteria at the prime $2$, and Riemann-Roch computations on modular curves and their quotients over finite fields.

papers.title: Torsion of elliptic curves over quartic number fields with rational $j$-invariant
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve defined over a quartic extension $K$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ with $j(E)\in\mathbb{Q}$. We classify the possible group structures of $E(K)_{\mathrm{tors}}$, concluding that the only additional possibilities, besides those occuring over quartic fields by base change from elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$, are $\mathbb{Z}/17\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}/21\mathbb{Z}$.

papers.title: Transversal unfoldings of derived foliations
papers.abstract: We study when a derived foliation along the fibres of a smooth morphism extends transversally to the total space. We classify strict unfoldings by basic Lie derivations, retaining the automorphisms arising from central isotropy. We define an intrinsic space of unfoldings and prove its agreement with the strict classification when the relative cotangent complex is a vector bundle in degree zero. A counterexample shows that the strict construction is not invariant under equivalent presentations. For two-term cotangent complexes, we describe cotangent extensions and their integrability conditions, and obtain cohomological existence criteria for strict unfoldings in explicit families. On smooth representable leaf spaces, descended unfoldings correspond to integrable Ehresmann connections.

papers.title: Tropical Degrees and Stable Intersections
papers.abstract: We study finite set-theoretic intersections of tropical curves with tropical hypersurfaces. An elementary divisor argument bounds their cardinality by the weighted sum of the Newton support function over the unbounded directions of the curve, without a transversality hypothesis. For tropical lines the bound is $h_\Delta(1,\dots,1)+\sum_i h_\Delta(-e_i)=n!\,\MV(\Delta,\Sigma,\dots,\Sigma)$. Explicit examples show that neither the $\ell^1$-diameter nor the support cardinality minus one gives a corresponding bound for tropical lines. We also record width refinements of the classical-line estimate of Lang, Shapiro and Shustin. A self-contained account of the standard transverse multiplicity formulas explains the role of saturated normal lattices and mixed-cell volumes. Finally, applying the tropical Bernstein theorem to locally independent subsystems gives a mixed-volume bound for the regular transverse locus of a redundant system. An example shows why a fixed subsystem need not compute the count on the whole redundant intersection.

papers.title: Twisted pencils of quartics, braid monodromy factorizations, and non-Hopfian Hurwitz curves
papers.abstract: We study which groups arise as fundamental groups of complements of affine Hurwitz curves. In every such group the product of the meridians is central and maps to the vector of component degrees in homology; this rules out, for instance, the Baumslag-Solitar groups $\operatorname{BS}(p,q)$ with $\lvert p\rvert\neq\lvert q\rvert$, and the groups of links with at least two components and vanishing linking numbers. O. V. Kulikova circumvented this obstruction for $\operatorname{BS}(2,3)$ by passing to the non-Hopfian group $\operatorname{BS}(2,3)\times\mathbb{Z}$, which Vik. S. Kulikov's doubling algorithm realizes in degree $768$. We give an explicit braid monodromy factorization of degree 12 with this group. The corresponding curve is not isotopic to an algebraic curve, yet it is obtained from a union of three quartics in a pencil by a single twist along a circle. More generally, for every closed braid $\hat\beta$ we realize $\pi_1(S^3\setminus\hat\beta)\times\mathbb{Z}$ by an explicit Hurwitz curve, again a twist of a union of quartics in a pencil. In the other direction, a Hurwitz curve with group $\operatorname{BS}(k,k+1)\times\mathbb{Z}$ has degree at least $4$, as every Hurwitz curve consisting of a conic and a line is H-isotopic to an algebraic one, after separation of its critical points. Finally, we show that certain semiholomorphic germs, among them those realizing the generalized Borromean rings, are braided surfaces but not Hurwitz curve germs.

papers.title: Unramified case of Colliot-Th\'el\`ene conjecture on quadratic forms
papers.abstract: The Colliot-Th\'el\`ene conjecture on quadratic forms asserts that any rationally isotropic nondegenerate quadratic form over a semilocal regular domain with $2$ invertible is isotropic. We prove the Colliot-Th\'el\`ene conjecture for semilocal regular domains that are geometrically regular over a discrete valuation ring with $2$ invertible. In particular, this includes unramified regular local rings of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, where $p\neq 2$.

papers.title: When is Polynomial Optimization SoS-Exact? Sufficient Regularization and Strict Gram Representations
papers.abstract: Global minimization of multivariate polynomials is computationally difficult in general, and nonnegativity does not necessarily imply a sum-of-squares (SoS) representation. We show that adding sufficiently strong Euclidean regularization to a polynomial provides a general mechanism for overcoming such challenges. Namely, for any multivariate polynomial $P$ of degree at most $p$ with a nonzero linear coefficient, and any even integer $2d>p$, we prove that $m_\sigma(s)=P(s)+\frac{\sigma}{2d}\|s\|_2^{2d}$ is SoS exact for all sufficiently large $\sigma$. Furthermore, the shifted polynomial $m_\sigma-\min m_\sigma$ admits a positive-definite Gram representation on appropriately-shifted nonconstant monomials. Consequently, the global minimum and minimizer can be recovered exactly by a single degree-$d$ semidefinite programming (SDP) representation, whose size is polynomial in the dimension for fixed $d$, without requiring higher levels of the SoS hierarchy. The proof develops a degree-independent mechanism based on the Bregman remainder of the regularizer: its strict Gram margin absorbs the lower-degree polynomial perturbations. We further establish an analogous exact SDP regime for polynomial optimization over sufficiently small Euclidean balls, connecting large regularization with small-radius trust-region problems. Finally, we investigate how the algebraic structure of the regularizer governs the existence of a strict Gram margin, extending the mechanism beyond Euclidean norms while identifying limitations of coordinate-separable regularization.

papers.title: Zero-cycles on quotients of multiple double covers and their products
papers.abstract: We prove the 0-cycle form of the generalized Bloch conjecture for smooth projective models of subgroup quotients of multiple double covers of projective space, with smooth branch hypersurfaces and reduced simple normal crossings branch divisor. Our integral character criterion yields, in every dimension at least four, simply connected varieties of general type with 0-cycle Chow group \(\mathbb{Z}\), canonical volume four, and no birational product decomposition. We also determine optimal integral supports for componentwise product quotients and character decompositions of degree zero Chow groups. Within this covering class, we classify the minimum volume models and compute their pluricanonical map degrees.
